# Plan format and label templates (proposed)

**Status:** proposed. Nothing here is implemented. This document details the
semantic core of the [compiled pattern language](README.md): the plan the
compiler emits beside value code, and the label templates from which the
runtime computes Contextual Flow Control (CFC) labels.

The label rules below change what CFC decides, so they are a semantic gap in
the sense of
[the correspondence procedure](../../development/cfc-spec-correspondence.md)
and are ruled on in `commonfabric/specs` before any of them binds the runtime.
This document describes the design and how this runtime would arrange it. It
cites the specification by section and chapter file. Where this document and a
ruling disagree, the ruling governs and this document is corrected.

The sibling documents are referred to by file name. `language-subset.md`
defines which source constructs lower to which operation, and
`builtin-inventory.md` places each built-in. `footprint-analysis.md` fills
in the record of a function body. `execution-and-storage.md` and
`scheduler-and-serving-loop.md` say how a plan is evaluated, stored and
scheduled. This document takes the operations as given and defines what
the plan records for them and what label each record yields.

## Notation

- `C(x)` is the confidentiality of `x`, a conjunction of clauses, and `I(x)`
  its integrity, a set of atoms (§3.1.1, §3.1.6, `03-core-concepts.md`).
- `a ⊔ b` joins confidentiality: the clauses of both, deduplicated under
  canonical equality (§3.1.2; §8.9.3, `08-09-runtime-label-propagation.md`,
  allows the deduplication).
- `a ⊓ b` is the class-aware integrity meet: the atoms present in both whose
  family is hereditary (§3.1.6.2, `03-core-concepts.md`: "Hereditary atoms
  survive **both combination and transformation** via intersection across
  inputs.").
- A **path** is a list of segments. A segment is a property name, or `*` for
  "each element", as in the stored envelope's entry paths. A well-known
  key is the segment of its string value: the key `[UI]` of a result is
  the segment `$UI`, and `[NAME]` is `$NAME` (the constants `UI` and
  `NAME` in `base/api/index.ts`).
- An **instance** is one running pattern with a result cell. A **cone** is a
  unit of evaluation. The compiler partitions what an instance computes
  into cones: every value is computed by exactly one cone, and a cone
  computes one or more outputs (section 1.4). A **cone instance** is one
  cone as it is evaluated for one scope instance and, inside element
  bodies, for one element key per enclosing collection
  (`execution-and-storage.md`, Terms). The body of an element construct is
  one or more cones, and an element key has one cone instance of each.
- A **cause** is what a transaction is opened for. There are four kinds: an
  event delivered to a handler, a set of changes, the completion of an
  effect, and a change of demand. A set of changes is the commits that
  arrived from storage, the commit of an effect's completion among them,
  and the writes of the events of a batch (section 5.4). The completion of
  an effect stores the effect's result in a commit of its own, and the
  derivations that read the result are evaluated in the transaction of the
  set of changes that commit joins (`scheduler-and-serving-loop.md` §10.2).
  A change of demand has a transaction of its own, which runs as the
  principal whose demand changed. Section 1.3 uses the word in a second
  sense, for what an identifier derives from, as in `.for(cause)`.

## 1. The plan

The plan is data. The compiler emits one plan per pattern, the runtime's CFC
kernel and scheduler read it, and no emitted code computes a label. Every
record is plain JSON so that it can be canonicalized and hashed.

### 1.1 Records

The declarations below are the whole format. Field comments state what a field
means and are part of the definition.

```ts
/** A path segment: a property name, or "*" for each element. */
export type Segment = string;
export type Path = readonly Segment[];

/** Content address of a canonicalized record (section 1.2). */
export type Hash = string;

/** Index into the array the field name says it indexes. */
export type Index = number;

/** A position in source, for diagnostics. */
export interface SourcePosition {
  readonly file: string;
  readonly start: number;
}

/**
 * The name of a record (section 1.3). A name of one part is a string. A
 * name of several parts is a record of its parts, and no string joins
 * them (section 1.2, "Written forms"). The member names are assumed.
 */
export type Name =
  | string
  /** One of several declarations of one name, by its ordinal from 1. */
  | { readonly name: string; readonly ordinal: number }
  /** A child that the site `site` of `Body.calls` of a body makes. */
  | { readonly body: Name; readonly site: Index }
  /** A cell that a body creates under a constant cause, with the cause. */
  | { readonly body: Name; readonly cause: unknown }
  /** A sidecar of a `wish` operation (section 3.19). */
  | { readonly operation: Name; readonly sidecar: string };

/**
 * One step of where a declaration sits. The steps of a declaration, outermost
 * first, are part of the cause its identifier derives from (section 1.3).
 */
export type WithinStep =
  /**
   * A call, compiled into this plan, of a pattern the compiler can see.
   * Provisional (P18): no record of a plan holds this step. It is a step
   * of the list that a record has at a call site, which the runtime
   * forms from the chain of sites (section 1.1, "A pattern compiled in
   * is written once").
   */
  | { readonly site: Name }
  /** The body of an element construct over a collection. */
  | { readonly element: Index };

export type ObservationClass =
  | "value"
  | "shape"
  | "enumeration"
  | "identity"
  /** The stored label of the path, not its content (section 2.4). */
  | "labelMetadata";

/** Where a slot's data lives. */
export type SlotRoot =
  /**
   * The instance's argument. Provisional (P18): in the record of a
   * pattern compiled in (`Plan.callees`), the argument of that pattern,
   * which each call site binds (`CallSite.argument`).
   */
  | { readonly kind: "argument" }
  /** A state cell of this instance (`Plan.stateCells`). */
  | { readonly kind: "state"; readonly cell: Index }
  /** The payload of the event a handler was invoked with. */
  | { readonly kind: "event"; readonly handler: Index }
  /** The current element of a collection (`Plan.collections`). */
  | { readonly kind: "element"; readonly collection: Index }
  /**
   * The position of the current element in the order a collection
   * iterates (`Plan.collections`). A slot with this root has the empty
   * path and observes `value`. Its label is the label of the collection's
   * array (section 2.2).
   */
  | { readonly kind: "index"; readonly collection: Index }
  /** The stored result of a durable operation (`Plan.operations`). */
  | { readonly kind: "operation"; readonly operation: Index }
  /** The result of a child instance (`Plan.children`). */
  | { readonly kind: "child"; readonly child: Index }
  /** The state a handler was bound to: its captures. */
  | { readonly kind: "binding"; readonly handler: Index }
  /** A property of the cause: path `eventKey` or `principal`. */
  | { readonly kind: "cause" }
  /** The private parameters a pattern closure was bound to (section 3.15). */
  | { readonly kind: "params" };

/** One input observed at one path in one way. */
export interface Slot {
  readonly root: SlotRoot;
  readonly path: Path;
  readonly observes: ObservationClass;
  /** Schema of the value at this path, by content address. */
  readonly schema: Hash;
  /**
   * For an `identity` slot: the reference is observed after resolution, at
   * the cell where the chain of links that starts at the path ends
   * (section 2.5).
   */
  readonly resolved?: true;
  /**
   * For a `shape` slot: the observation is made in place. It observes
   * whether the position the path names holds anything, a link included,
   * and does not continue through a link stored there. A `shape` slot at a
   * position of handle type, or of reference type, has it (section 2.5).
   */
  readonly inPlace?: true;
  /**
   * The read is made with `sample()`. It is in the label, and a change at
   * the slot's address does not make a cone stale (section 2.5).
   */
  readonly sampled?: true;
  /**
   * The label the schema declares for this observation, when it declares
   * one. A declared label is what makes a constraint checkable at compile
   * time (section 4.4).
   */
  readonly declared?: DeclaredLabel;
}

export interface DeclaredLabel {
  readonly confidentiality?: readonly unknown[];
  readonly integrity?: readonly unknown[];
}

/**
 * A label in symbolic form. Each node kind has a confidentiality rule and an
 * integrity rule (section 3).
 */
export type Template =
  /** A literal or frozen module-scope datum. Contributes nothing. */
  | { readonly op: "const" }
  /** The observation of one slot, passed through unchanged. */
  | { readonly op: "slot"; readonly slot: Index }
  /**
   * The template of another output of the plan (`Plan.outputs`), named
   * and not written out. By ruling every input of a node that is an
   * output of the plan, kept or interim, is this node, and no template
   * holds a copy of the template of another output. The node denotes the
   * label that the named output's `template` denotes, so a template with
   * each such node replaced by the template it names has the same label
   * (section 3.2, "A reference to an output"). Provisional (P18): with
   * `site`, the node names an entry of the `outputs` of the callee of
   * that call site (`sites` of the record that holds the node), and
   * denotes the label of that entry for the cone instances of the site.
   * Every other member of a record that names an output by `output`
   * takes `site` in the same way.
   */
  | { readonly op: "output"; readonly output: Index; readonly site?: Index }
  /**
   * An entry of the plan's template table (`Plan.templates`), named and
   * not written out. Provisional (P6): a template that is larger than
   * one leaf node and stands at more than one position of a plan is
   * written once, in the table, and each position holds this node. The
   * node denotes the label that the entry denotes for the inputs of the
   * place that holds the node, so a template with each such node
   * replaced by its entry has the same label (section 3.2, "A template
   * written once").
   */
  | { readonly op: "shared"; readonly template: Index }
  /**
   * A new value computed from the inputs. A join of templates is this
   * node with `by: { expression: true }` over the joined templates
   * (section 3.2). An input that is an output of the plan is an `output`
   * node.
   */
  | {
    readonly op: "derive";
    readonly inputs: readonly Template[];
    /**
     * What computed it: a sandboxed body, or emitted expression code. For
     * expression code, `pattern` names the pattern in whose source the
     * expression is written (`Plan.patterns`). It is absent where that is
     * entry 0, the pattern the plan is compiled from (section 3.2).
     */
    readonly by:
      | { readonly body: Index }
      | { readonly expression: true; readonly pattern?: Index };
  }
  /**
   * Conditional selection. One of three nodes whose label depends on a
   * value, with a `fold` that has `through` and a `pick`.
   */
  | {
    readonly op: "select";
    readonly selector: Index;
    readonly condition: Template;
    readonly branches: readonly Template[];
  }
  /**
   * A join over the elements of a collection: all of them, or, when
   * `through` is set, the leading elements up to and including the position
   * that selector holds. The runtime supplies that position from its own
   * scan (section 3.13). `collection` is the record of the construct whose
   * callback `body` is the template of: `body` is over the `element` slots
   * that name that record. The membership the node joins is the one that
   * record iterates, which is the membership of its `source`, and not its
   * own `membership` (section 3.2).
   */
  | {
    readonly op: "fold";
    readonly collection: Index;
    readonly body: Template;
    readonly through?: Index;
    /** The pattern the construct is written in, as for a `derive`. */
    readonly pattern?: Index;
  }
  /**
   * One child chosen by a run-time key: an element of a collection, a child
   * of a container slot, or a child of a container the instance computed
   * (`Plan.outputs`). `pick` is the node's own choice point
   * (`Plan.picks`), as `selector` is a `select`'s. `body` is over the
   * chosen child's slots, and for a computed container it is the `output`
   * node of the entry that has the label of the chosen child (section
   * 3.18).
   */
  | {
    readonly op: "pick";
    readonly pick: Index;
    readonly from:
      | { readonly collection: Index }
      | { readonly container: Index }
      | { readonly output: Index; readonly site?: Index };
    readonly choice: Template;
    readonly body: Template;
  }
  /** Reads whose addresses are known only at run time. */
  | { readonly op: "dynamic"; readonly reads: Index };

/**
 * A selection point: which branch of a `select` the value code took. A
 * selector that a `fold` names in `through` holds a position instead. The
 * runtime supplies it from its own scan, and the value code reports nothing
 * for it (section 3.13).
 */
export interface Selector {
  /**
   * Number of branches. The value code reports an index below this. For
   * the `through` of a `fold` it is 0, and no `Cone.selectors` lists the
   * selector, because no value function reports it.
   */
  readonly arity: number;
}

/**
 * A choice point: which child a `pick` chose. Two `pick` nodes are two
 * choice points, also where they choose from one container
 * (section 3.18).
 */
export interface Pick {
  /**
   * Who supplies the choice. `runtime`: the runtime chooses an element of a
   * collection from per-element results, and knows the element's key.
   * `valueCode`: the value code reports the key of the child it chose in a
   * container, or that it chose none. A choice point with `runtime` is in
   * no `Cone.picks`, because no value function reports it.
   */
  readonly chosenBy: "runtime" | "valueCode";
}

/**
 * A collection the instance maps, filters, scans, or folds over. Each
 * construct with a callback has a record of its own (sections 3.6, 3.7,
 * 3.8, 3.13 and 3.17). The record holds one thing about element keys,
 * `keyFields`. The element part of a key and its occurrence count follow
 * from the elements at run time, and the position is in no key (section
 * 1.3). Which nodes
 * of a body read the index is recorded where each node lists its slots:
 * a slot of root `index` that names this record.
 */
export interface Collection {
  /** The name an `element` step refers to it by (section 1.3). */
  readonly name: Name;
  readonly within: readonly WithinStep[];
  /**
   * The construct the record is of. It says what the runtime does with
   * the per-element results: assembles them (`map`, `filter`, `flatMap`),
   * scans them (`some`, `every`, `find`, `findIndex`), or hands them to the
   * operation whose `input` has a `fold` that names this record
   * (`operation`: an aggregate with a callback, a `reduce`, or an index).
   */
  readonly construct:
    | "map"
    | "filter"
    | "flatMap"
    | "some"
    | "every"
    | "find"
    | "findIndex"
    | "operation";
  /**
   * What the construct iterates: its receiver. The record of a scan, an
   * aggregate, a `reduce` or an index names a slot, a bucket, or an
   * output, which for a receiver that is itself a collection of the plan
   * is that collection's assembled output (section 3.13). The record of a
   * `map`, a `filter` or a `flatMap` whose receiver is itself the result
   * of one of those three names that collection's record, with `via`.
   */
  readonly source:
    | { readonly slot: Index }
    /**
     * `collection` is the record of the receiver. `via` is the construct
     * of this record, the one applied to the receiver, and equals
     * `construct`: it says how the elements of this collection come from
     * those of the receiver (section 3.7).
     */
    | {
      readonly collection: Index;
      readonly via: "map" | "filter" | "flatMap";
    }
    /** A bucket of a collection index (`Plan.operations`). */
    | { readonly operation: Index }
    /** An array the instance computed (`Plan.outputs`). */
    | { readonly output: Index; readonly site?: Index };
  /**
   * The key fields that the type of the receiver declares with
   * `ArrayByKey<T, "a" | "b">`, where it declares any: the names of
   * properties of the element, in the order of the names. It is a copy
   * of the keyword `keyFields` of the schema of the receiver's array,
   * held here so that the runtime forms the keys of a source that is an
   * output, of which the plan holds no schema. The runtime forms the
   * keys of the element table with it, and resolves no reference by key
   * with it: a key that names its fields is resolved from the key
   * alone. An element that is a plain value is keyed by the values of
   * those properties, and a position that holds a link is keyed by its
   * cell (section 1.3, "A declared key field"). Absent where `source`
   * names a collection: an element then has the upstream key. Where
   * the type of the receiver is a plain array type in a pattern that
   * is compiled in, the member holds the key fields that the type of
   * the caller's place declares, or that the type of the argument
   * expression declares where the caller gives a computed value
   * (*assumed*, section 8, question 149). Provisional (P18): the
   * record of a pattern compiled in then leaves the member absent, and
   * the entry of `CallSite.argument` that binds the receiver holds the
   * key fields of that call. Absent where none of these declares a key.
   * By ruling the runtime then forms the keys with the key fields of
   * the array that the receiver holds, where the schema that is
   * traversed while the link to that array is resolved declares any
   * (section 8, questions 143 and 145).
   */
  readonly keyFields?: readonly string[];
  /**
   * The label of which elements the result of the construct has and in
   * what order. For a scan and for `operation` it is the membership the
   * record iterates (section 3.7). Where that is the template of an
   * output of the plan, as for a record whose `source` names an output,
   * it is the `output` node of that entry (section 3.2, "A reference to
   * an output").
   */
  readonly membership: Template;
}

/**
 * One use of a sandboxed function body and the result of footprint analysis.
 * Two calls of one function in the reactive tier are two records with the
 * same `code`. A handler is one record however many bindings name it.
 */
export interface Body {
  /** Content address of the body's source as the loader receives it. */
  readonly code: Hash;
  /** The name of this use, and where it sits (section 1.3). */
  readonly name: Name;
  readonly within: readonly WithinStep[];
  readonly kind:
    | "lift"
    | "computed"
    | "action"
    | "handler"
    | "assert"
    /** An authored module-scope function called from the reactive tier. */
    | "function"
    /** A function of an imported TypeScript module; its body is opaque. */
    | "imported";
  /**
   * Slots the runtime materializes into the body's argument, each with
   * its place there.
   */
  readonly reads: readonly ReadInput[];
  /**
   * What the body observes of values the instance computed: the result of
   * another body, or of expression code (section 3.9).
   */
  readonly computed: readonly ComputedInput[];
  /**
   * The cell handles through which the body makes a read that no slot of
   * `reads` covers. Such a read is journaled while the body runs and enters
   * the label as a `dynamic` template. A handle the body only passes on,
   * writes through, or reads at slots of `reads` is not listed
   * (section 3.9).
   */
  readonly handles: readonly HandleReads[];
  /** The statically known targets the body writes, with their constraints. */
  readonly writes: readonly WriteEdge[];
  /** Where the body's writes that have no static target may land. */
  readonly envelopes: readonly WriteEnvelope[];
  /**
   * Result paths that are not plainly computed from the whole footprint
   * (section 3.9). A path with no entry is computed.
   */
  readonly outputs: readonly BodyOutput[];
  /** The runtime calls the body can make (section 3.14). */
  readonly calls: readonly BodyCall[];
  /** Where analysis gave up, for diagnostics (section 2.2). */
  readonly widenings: readonly Widening[];
}

/** One slot a body reads, and where its value is placed. */
export interface ReadInput {
  /** The slot (`Plan.slots`). */
  readonly slot: Index;
  /**
   * The path in the body's argument at which the slot's value is placed,
   * formed as `ComputedInput.at` is. For a handler the first segment is
   * `event` for the first parameter and `binding` for the second, and
   * the slot's path follows. For a slot that a static read through a
   * handle reads, the path is the place of the handle followed by the
   * path below the handle's cell (section 3.9).
   */
  readonly at: Path;
  /**
   * For an entry of a body of a pattern compiled in, whose slot is a
   * slot of the caller that the call bound a path of the callee's
   * argument to: the default the callee declares for that path. The
   * runtime puts it at `at` where the slot yields nothing and no place
   * the slot resolves through declares a default of its own (section
   * 1.1). Absent where the callee declares none.
   */
  readonly default?: unknown;
}

/** One path of a computed value that a body observes in one way. */
export interface ComputedInput {
  /**
   * Where the value sits in the body's argument. For an authored function
   * the first segment is the name of the parameter the value is passed
   * for, and for a `computed` the name of the captured variable. A `lift`
   * has one parameter, and the path starts below it.
   */
  readonly at: Path;
  readonly observes: ObservationClass;
  /**
   * The label of what the body observes there. Where the value is an
   * output of the plan, an `output` node, or the join of the `output`
   * nodes of its entries at and below the path (section 3.9).
   */
  readonly template: Template;
}

/**
 * A reference a body was given, named by where it reached the body: the
 * index of an `identity` slot, or an `identity` entry of that body's
 * `computed`, for a handle, a container or a factory value that reached the
 * body in a value the instance computed. The body is the one whose record
 * holds the name: for a `Binding`, a `Closure` or a `Child`, the body whose
 * site refers to it. A record of the reactive tier, which no site of a body
 * refers to, names a slot.
 */
export type GivenReference = Index | { readonly computed: Index };

/**
 * An `identity` entry of the `computed` of one body of the plan, where a
 * record of the plan and not of that body names it.
 */
export interface ComputedReference {
  readonly body: Index;
  readonly computed: Index;
}

/** A cell handle a body reads through at run time. */
export interface HandleReads {
  /**
   * The handle: its `identity` slot, an entry of `Body.reads`, or an entry
   * of `Body.computed` of class `identity` for a reference the instance
   * computed. A slot whose path has a `*` stands for every handle those
   * positions hold. `call` names a site of `Body.calls` that makes
   * something a later invocation of the body can find again: an
   * `instantiate` site of a body that is re-evaluated, an `instantiate`
   * site that is `identifiedBy: "tag"`, or a `createCell` site that is
   * `identifiedBy: "cause"`. The entry stands for the links to the
   * instances, or the handles to the cells, that site makes (sections 3.9
   * and 3.14).
   */
  readonly handle:
    | { readonly slot: Index }
    | { readonly computed: Index }
    | { readonly call: Index };
  /**
   * The read envelope: the schema every read through the handle is made
   * under. It admits the paths below the handle's cell that some read
   * through the handle may observe, each with its class, and nothing else.
   * Where it admits a position as a handle, the body may read through the
   * handle it finds there, and what the schema admits below that position
   * is the envelope of those reads (section 3.9).
   */
  readonly envelope: Hash;
}

/** How one path of a body's result relates to the body's inputs. */
export interface BodyOutput {
  readonly path: Path;
  /**
   * `passes`: the reference at this path is always one reference the body
   * was given, at an `identity` slot or at an `identity` entry of
   * `Body.computed`. `passes` names an entry whose path has no `*`.
   * `oneOf`: it is always one of several such references. An entry whose
   * path has a `*` stands for several references, so a reference taken
   * from it is named in `oneOf`, also where it is the only entry named.
   * The runtime verifies either by reference identity (section 3.9).
   */
  readonly reference?:
    | { readonly passes: GivenReference }
    | { readonly oneOf: readonly GivenReference[] };
  /** The result schema requires the path, so its existence is constant. */
  readonly required?: true;
}

/**
 * A site in a body that makes a runtime call. A site can run any number of
 * times in one invocation; each occurrence gets its own identifier
 * (section 1.3).
 */
export type BodyCall =
  /**
   * Instantiates a pattern and returns a link to the instance. `order`
   * identifies an occurrence by its order: among the requests of a
   * handler's invocation, or, in a body that is re-evaluated, among the
   * instantiations one evaluation makes at this site. `tag` identifies it
   * by the value given to `.for(...)` (section 1.3).
   */
  | {
    readonly kind: "instantiate";
    readonly child: Index;
    readonly identifiedBy: "order" | "tag";
  }
  /**
   * Creates a cell and returns a handle to it. Where the cause is a
   * constant, or the element key of the enclosing element body, in a body
   * that is re-evaluated, the cell is a state cell of the plan, and
   * `stateCell` names it (`Plan.stateCells`, section 3.14).
   */
  | {
    readonly kind: "createCell";
    readonly schema: Hash;
    readonly scope: "space" | "user" | "session";
    readonly identifiedBy: "order" | "cause";
    readonly stateCell?: Index;
  }
  /** Requests an effectful built-in and returns a link to its result. */
  | { readonly kind: "effect"; readonly builtin: string }
  /** Binds a handler to captured values and returns its stream. */
  | { readonly kind: "bind"; readonly binding: Index };

/** One place where footprint analysis gave up, and what covers it. */
export interface Widening {
  /**
   * The slots of `Body.reads` that stand for more than the body reads: a
   * `value` slot over a subtree, or the slots at `*` that stand for one
   * child the analysis could not name, with the `enumeration` slot of the
   * keyed container.
   */
  readonly slots: readonly Index[];
  /**
   * The entries of `Body.computed` that stand for more than the body reads,
   * in the same two ways, the `enumeration` entry of the keyed container
   * included, where the widened input is a value the instance computed.
   */
  readonly computed?: readonly Index[];
  /**
   * An entry of `Body.handles` the analysis lost track of. Its envelope is
   * then the handle's whole declared type.
   */
  readonly handle?: Index;
  /** Source position of the expression that caused it. */
  readonly at: SourcePosition;
}

/** A statically known write target of a body or cone. */
export interface WriteEdge {
  readonly target:
    | { readonly kind: "output"; readonly path: Path }
    | { readonly kind: "state"; readonly cell: Index; readonly path: Path }
    /**
     * The cell a handle links to, at a path below the handle's. `slot` is
     * the handle's `identity` slot: a handle in the event, in the state a
     * handler was bound to, in the argument, or in an element. With
     * `resolved`, the write is made through what `resolveAsCell()` returns
     * for the handle, and it lands in the cell where that resolution ends
     * (section 3.11).
     */
    | {
      readonly kind: "handle";
      readonly slot: Index;
      readonly path: Path;
      readonly resolved?: true;
    }
    /**
     * The same, for a handle that reached the writing body in a value the
     * instance computed. `computed` is the handle's `identity` entry of
     * that body's `computed`. The plan has no root and path for the cell
     * (section 3.11).
     */
    | {
      readonly kind: "handle";
      readonly computed: Index;
      readonly path: Path;
      readonly resolved?: true;
    }
    /** The argument document of a child instance. */
    | { readonly kind: "argument"; readonly child: Index; readonly path: Path }
    /**
     * What a site of the body made (`Body.calls`): the cell of a
     * `createCell` site, or the stream of a `bind` site, for an event the
     * body sends on it (section 3.11).
     */
    | { readonly kind: "created"; readonly call: Index; readonly path: Path }
    /**
     * The stored request of an effect: of an operation of the plan, or of
     * an `effect` site of the body (`Body.calls`). For an operation of
     * kind `wish`, the stored operands, and for one of kind `reduce`, the
     * initial value at the path `initial` (sections 3.13 and 3.19).
     */
    | {
      readonly kind: "request";
      readonly of: { readonly operation: Index } | { readonly call: Index };
      readonly path: Path;
    }
    /** The anchors document of the field at an `identity` slot. */
    | { readonly kind: "anchors"; readonly of: Index };
  /**
   * The label of the value written. Where the value, or an input of the
   * template, is an output of the plan, an `output` node and no copy
   * (section 3.2, "A reference to an output").
   */
  readonly template: Template;
  /**
   * The value written at the target is a reference the body was given, as
   * `BodyOutput.reference` says of a result path. The runtime verifies it
   * by identity, and `template` applies where the check fails. In a
   * handler the link written carries `template` joined with the
   * reference's own label also where the check holds (section 3.9).
   */
  readonly reference?:
    | { readonly passes: GivenReference }
    | { readonly oneOf: readonly GivenReference[] };
  readonly constraints: readonly Index[];
}

/** Where writes that have no static target may land (section 3.11). */
export type WriteEnvelope =
  /**
   * At or below a path of the cell a handle links to. A `*` segment of
   * `path` stands for a child the analysis could not name. A slot whose own
   * path has a `*` stands for every cell an element links to. For a handle
   * the body finds by a read through another handle, `slot` is an
   * `identity` slot at the position where the handle is found, whose path
   * crosses the first handle's link. That slot is in no `reads`: it names
   * the place, is not materialized, and joins no template. `resolved` is
   * as for a `WriteEdge`.
   */
  | {
    readonly kind: "handle";
    readonly slot: Index;
    readonly path: Path;
    readonly resolved?: true;
  }
  /**
   * The same, for a handle that reached the body in a value the instance
   * computed: `computed` is its `identity` entry of the body's `computed`.
   * An entry whose own path has a `*` stands for every cell those
   * positions link to. For a handle the body finds by a read through the
   * entry's handle, `found` is the position where it is found: a path
   * below the cell the entry's handle links to, with `*` at each segment
   * the analysis cannot name. It is resolved as the path of an `identity`
   * slot is, so it crosses the link of a handle found on the way and stops
   * at its last segment. `path` is then at or below the cell the found
   * handle links to, and `resolved` applies to the found handle
   * (section 3.11).
   */
  | {
    readonly kind: "handle";
    readonly computed: Index;
    readonly found?: Path;
    readonly path: Path;
    readonly resolved?: true;
  }
  /**
   * A cell a `createCell` site creates under a cause computed from data,
   * or a cell reached through the link an `instantiate` or an `effect`
   * site returned (section 3.11).
   */
  | { readonly kind: "created"; readonly call: Index };

/** A set of reads resolved at run time. */
export interface DynamicReads {
  readonly why:
    /**
     * The links followed from a reference: the one at an `identity` slot,
     * one that reached a body in a value the instance computed, or, for a
     * call in the reactive tier, one that is an output of the instance
     * (`Plan.outputs`, section 3.16).
     */
    | {
      readonly kind: "link";
      readonly through:
        | Index
        | ComputedReference
        | { readonly output: Index; readonly site?: Index };
    }
    /** Reads through an entry of that body's `handles`. */
    | { readonly kind: "handle"; readonly body: Index; readonly handle: Index }
    /**
     * The access list of the space an `identity` slot's target lives in, or
     * of the space a `value` slot names. For an operand that reached a body
     * in a value the instance computed, its entry of that body's `computed`.
     * For an operand of a call in the reactive tier that the instance
     * computed, its output (`Plan.outputs`, section 3.16).
     */
    | {
      readonly kind: "space";
      readonly of:
        | Index
        | ComputedReference
        | { readonly output: Index; readonly site?: Index };
    }
    /**
     * The reads a `wish` made of what no slot names while it resolved its
     * target: the links it followed, the tests of whether a target holds
     * anything, and the name and schema of every candidate a search
     * considered. `operation` is the wish (`Plan.operations`,
     * section 3.19).
     */
    | { readonly kind: "search"; readonly operation: Index }
    /**
     * Label-metadata observations a body made of targets no slot names
     * (section 3.16).
     */
    | { readonly kind: "labelMetadata"; readonly body: Index };
}

/**
 * What an input constraint is evaluated on: the inputs of the guarded
 * write's body whose path overlaps the annotated path (section 4.4).
 */
export interface ConstraintInputs {
  /** Slots of `Body.reads`, or of `Cone.slots` (section 1.5). */
  readonly slots: readonly Index[];
  /**
   * Entries of `Body.handles` through which the body reads the annotated
   * path. `path` is the annotated path below the handle's cell. The
   * constraint is evaluated on the journaled reads through the entry
   * whose path overlaps it, in either prefix direction.
   */
  readonly handles?: readonly {
    readonly body: Index;
    readonly handle: Index;
    readonly path: Path;
  }[];
  /**
   * Entries of `Body.computed`, of any class, whose path overlaps the
   * annotated path. The constraint is evaluated on each entry's template,
   * instantiated.
   */
  readonly computed?: readonly {
    readonly body: Index;
    readonly computed: Index;
  }[];
}

/** A requirement on inputs or on a write (section 4.4). */
export type Constraint =
  | ({
    readonly kind: "requiredIntegrity";
    readonly patterns: readonly unknown[];
  } & ConstraintInputs)
  | ({
    readonly kind: "maxConfidentiality";
    readonly ceiling: readonly unknown[];
  } & ConstraintInputs)
  | { readonly kind: "writeFloor"; readonly patterns: readonly unknown[] }
  | { readonly kind: "writerFit" }
  | { readonly kind: "writer"; readonly anyOf: readonly WriterPolicy[] };

export interface WriterPolicy {
  /** The body that may write, by content address. */
  readonly body?: Hash;
  /** The UI contract an event has to satisfy for this alternative. */
  readonly uiContract?: {
    readonly helper: "UiAction" | "UiPromptSlot" | "UiDisclosure";
    readonly action?: string;
    readonly trustedPattern?: string;
    readonly requiredEventIntegrity?: readonly string[];
  };
}

/** One output path of the instance and how its value and label are made. */
export interface Output {
  /**
   * For a kept output, its path in the result. For an interim output, a
   * path below the value `interim` names.
   */
  readonly path: Path;
  /** The name of the interim value this is a path of (section 1.3). */
  readonly interim?: string;
  /**
   * The cone that computes the value. For the assembled result of an
   * element construct, which no cone computes, see `collection`.
   */
  readonly cone: Index;
  /**
   * The output is the assembled result of this element construct
   * (`Plan.collections`). The runtime assembles the value and no value
   * function returns it. `path` is the path of the collection itself,
   * `template` is the collection's membership template, and `cone` is the
   * last cone of the construct's body in the order of `Plan.cones`
   * (section 1.4). For a scan, the output is the scan's result, which
   * the runtime produces from the per-element results, and `template` is
   * the scan's template (section 3.13).
   */
  readonly collection?: Index;
  /**
   * The value of the output is, on every evaluation, the assembled
   * result of this element construct (`Plan.collections`), passed on
   * unchanged from the output that has it as `collection`. By ruling
   * the output is the same collection for keying: a record whose
   * `source` names this output has the element keys of that collection
   * and the places its elements came from (section 1.3).
   */
  readonly passesCollection?: Index;
  /**
   * The key fields that the type of the output's value declares with
   * `ArrayByKey<T, "a" | "b">`, where the value is an array whose type
   * declares any: the names, in the order of the names. It is a copy, as
   * `Collection.keyFields` is. The plan holds no schema of an output, so
   * the runtime forms from this member the schema of the link that it
   * writes where the output is given whole to an instance of its own:
   * an array schema with the keyword `keyFields` (section 3.15, "Labels
   * going in"). For the assembled result of a `map` it is present only
   * where the element type of the result has those properties (section
   * 1.3, "A declared key field"). The member is assumed (section 8,
   * questions 149 and 155).
   */
  readonly keyFields?: readonly string[];
  readonly template: Template;
  /** Whether the path is reachable from the result cell. */
  readonly kept: boolean;
  /**
   * The scope the plan knows the value to have. The scope at run time is
   * this one or a narrower one (section 1.4). Absent means `space`.
   */
  readonly scope?: "user" | "session";
  readonly constraints: readonly Index[];
}

/** One dependency cone: a unit of evaluation. */
export interface Cone {
  /** Name of the emitted value function for this cone. */
  readonly entry: string;
  /** Content address of that function's emitted source. */
  readonly code: Hash;
  /** Where the cone's code begins in source, for diagnostics. */
  readonly at: SourcePosition;
  /**
   * Where the cone's code is written. Its `element` steps, outermost
   * first, are the collections of the element bodies the cone is written
   * in. By ruling the runtime takes two things from them: an instance of
   * the cone exists for each combination of element keys of those
   * collections, and what an instance holds is kept under those keys
   * (section 1.4). That the member holds the `site` steps as well is
   * assumed (section 8, question 98).
   */
  readonly within: readonly WithinStep[];
  /**
   * Every slot the value function receives, over all selections. The runtime
   * passes these, the outputs its incoming edges name, and nothing else
   * (sections 1.4 and 7).
   */
  readonly slots: readonly Index[];
  readonly bodies: readonly Index[];
  /** The selectors whose branch the value function reports. */
  readonly selectors: readonly Index[];
  /**
   * The choice points of the `pick` nodes the cone evaluates whose key the
   * value function reports (`chosenBy: "valueCode"`).
   */
  readonly picks: readonly Index[];
  /** Side-writes this cone performs besides its outputs. */
  readonly writes: readonly WriteEdge[];
  /**
   * Whether the cone's interim outputs are stored as a cache: always, or
   * never. Absent means the runtime decides (section 1.4).
   */
  readonly cache?: "always" | "never";
}

/** An edge between cones: `from` writes something `to` reads. */
export interface ConeEdge {
  readonly from: Index;
  readonly to: Index;
  readonly via:
    /**
     * An output of `from` that the value function of `to` receives.
     * Provisional (P18): with `site`, the output is an entry of the
     * `outputs` of the callee of that call site, and `from` indexes the
     * `cones` of that callee. No edge is written for an output of this
     * record that a call site binds a path of its callee's argument to:
     * the entry of `CallSite.argument` is that edge.
     */
    | { readonly kind: "output"; readonly output: Index; readonly site?: Index }
    | { readonly kind: "state"; readonly cell: Index; readonly path: Path }
    /**
     * A cell `from` writes through a handle (`WriteEdge` target `handle`),
     * which a slot of `to` with the same root and an overlapping path reads.
     * `resolved` is as the write edge has it. A target that names its
     * handle by `computed` has no edge of this kind (section 3.11).
     */
    | {
      readonly kind: "handle";
      readonly slot: Index;
      readonly path: Path;
      readonly resolved?: true;
    };
}

/** A state cell and the cause its identifier derives from. */
export interface StateCell {
  /**
   * The name the cell's creation is caused by. For a cell that a
   * `createCell` site of a re-evaluated body creates under a constant
   * cause, or under the element key, the name is formed from the body's
   * `name` and the cause, and `within` is the body's (section 3.14).
   */
  readonly name: Name;
  readonly scope: "space" | "user" | "session";
  /**
   * Where the cell is declared. Each `element` step adds that element's key
   * to the cause, so the cell is one per occurrence of an element (section
   * 1.3).
   */
  readonly within: readonly WithinStep[];
  /**
   * The schema of the cell's value. Where the declaration gives the cell
   * a first value that is a constant, the schema holds it as its default,
   * and nothing is written when the cell is created (section 1.3).
   */
  readonly schema: Hash;
  /**
   * For a cell whose declaration gives it a first value that is not a
   * constant: the write edge that writes it, an entry of `writes` of the
   * cone that computes the value, with target `state`. The runtime
   * performs that edge once, when the cell is first created, and not on
   * a later evaluation of the cone (section 1.3).
   */
  readonly first?: { readonly cone: Index; readonly write: Index };
}

/** An operation with durable state of its own. */
export interface Operation {
  readonly kind:
    | "effect"
    | "aggregate"
    | "reduce"
    | "index"
    | "cache"
    | "materializer"
    /**
     * A `wish`. It is structural: it has no request transaction and no
     * egress check, and the runtime resolves it in the transaction that
     * evaluates a reader of its result (section 3.19).
     */
    | "wish"
    /**
     * A `sqliteDatabase` declaration. It has no request and no
     * transaction of its own, and its state is the database's handle
     * (section 3.14).
     */
    | "database";
  /**
   * What implements it: a built-in; a body, which for a materializer is
   * the body whose `writes` and `envelopes` are its declared write envelope
   * (section 3.11); for a forced cache, the cone whose outputs it
   * stores; or, for a `reduce`, the cone of its step expression
   * (section 3.13). An aggregate, an index, an effect and a `wish` name a
   * built-in.
   */
  readonly implementation:
    | { readonly builtin: string }
    | { readonly body: Index }
    | { readonly cone: Index };
  /**
   * The label of what the operation works from: for an effect, the join of
   * the templates of its request; for an aggregate, a `reduce` or an index,
   * the folded input; for a `wish`, the join of the templates of its
   * operands; for a cache, the join over the slots of the cached
   * cone; for a materializer, the template of its body; for a database,
   * `const`, because its table declarations are constants of the plan. It
   * is also the label of the operation's bookkeeping state (section 2.6).
   * Each joined template that is an output of the plan is an `output`
   * node (section 3.2, "A reference to an output").
   */
  readonly input: Template;
  /**
   * A scope the operation has whatever the scope of the cone instance that
   * computes its request. For an effect, the scope its built-in declares
   * where it needs a requester or a reader, as `agent`, `navigateTo` and a
   * `sqliteQuery` on a database in another space or with `readClearance`
   * do (`builtin-inventory.md`, "The requester of a request"): the
   * operation then has a unit per demanding principal or session. For a
   * `wish`, `user` where its target can lie in the home space of the
   * demanding principal (section 3.19). For a
   * database, the scope the declared type of the handle gives. Absent, the
   * operation has the scope of that cone instance, and a database has
   * `space`.
   */
  readonly scope?: "user" | "session";
  /**
   * For a database: the table declarations, with the label rules they
   * hold, in the canonical form of the constant the source gives.
   */
  readonly tables?: unknown;
  /** The cause its state document's identifier derives from. */
  readonly name: Name;
  readonly within: readonly WithinStep[];
}

/**
 * A pattern instantiated with a plan of its own: a pattern received as a
 * factory value, any pattern a function body instantiates, or a pattern
 * called through `asInstance()` or `inSpace(...)` in the reactive tier
 * (section 3.15).
 */
export interface Child {
  /**
   * The pattern: known at compile time; a factory value, named by its
   * `identity` slot or, where it reached the instantiating body in a value
   * the instance computed, by its `identity` entry of that body's
   * `computed`; or an inline pattern written as the callee of an
   * instantiation in a body, with what it captures (`Plan.closures`).
   */
  readonly callee:
    | { readonly compiled: Hash }
    | { readonly factory: GivenReference }
    | { readonly closure: Index };
  /** Declared by the callee's type; what the enclosing plan checks against. */
  readonly argumentSchema: Hash;
  readonly resultSchema: Hash;
  /** The cause the instance's identifier derives from. */
  readonly name: Name;
  readonly within: readonly WithinStep[];
  /**
   * `asInstance()`: the call is an instance of its own by the author's
   * declaration. Under an `element` step of `within` the instance is
   * not torn down when its key leaves the collection, and an event for
   * one of its streams is handled while the key is away (section
   * 3.15). The form of the member is assumed.
   */
  readonly asInstance?: true;
  /** `asScope`: the scope of the state the instance declares. */
  readonly scope?: "space" | "user" | "session";
  /** `inSpace`: the target space and the options of the request. */
  readonly space?: SpaceRequest;
}

/** What an `inSpace` request records (section 3.14). */
export interface SpaceRequest {
  /** Which space the instance is created in. */
  readonly target:
    /** A space identifier. */
    | { readonly kind: "identifier"; readonly space: RequestValue }
    /**
     * The space a cell lives in. The cell is named by its `identity` slot
     * or, where it reached the requesting body in a value the instance
     * computed, by its `identity` entry of that body's `computed`.
     */
    | { readonly kind: "spaceOf"; readonly cell: GivenReference }
    /** A name the calling space resolves. */
    | { readonly kind: "name"; readonly name: RequestValue }
    /** A space of the site's own, which has no name. */
    | { readonly kind: "anonymous" };
  /** The options written at the site. An absent member was not written. */
  readonly grants?: RequestValue;
  readonly root?: RequestValue;
  readonly spaceKind?: RequestValue;
  readonly selfOwned?: RequestValue;
}

/**
 * A value of an `inSpace` request: a constant of the site, a slot, or a
 * value the requesting body computes, which carries that body's template.
 * The request consumes the value, so the slot is of class `value`, over
 * the subtree where the value is a container. A value that is one
 * projection of an input bound to a value the instance computed has no
 * slot and is recorded as `body` (section 3.14).
 */
export type RequestValue =
  | { readonly constant: unknown }
  | { readonly slot: Index }
  | { readonly body: Index };

/**
 * A pattern closure: an inline pattern bound to what it captures
 * (section 3.15). Used as a value, it is what a `factory` slot holds when
 * the factory was written in this plan. Written as the callee of an
 * instantiation in a body, it is the callee of a `Child`.
 */
export interface Closure {
  /** The compiled identity of the inline pattern. */
  readonly pattern: Hash;
  /** What is bound to each path of the pattern's private parameters. */
  readonly params: readonly {
    readonly path: Path;
    /** An `output` node where the bound value is an output of the plan. */
    readonly template: Template;
    /**
     * For a closure used as a value: a data value is copied into the
     * factory value, and a cell stays a link. For the callee of an
     * instantiation in a body, as `Binding.state` has it for a binding
     * made in a body. No class is recorded for a copied path: the copy
     * holds what the slots with root `params` of the inline pattern's
     * plan observe of it (section 3.15).
     */
    readonly capture: "copy" | "link";
    /** As `Binding.state` has it. */
    readonly reference?:
      | { readonly passes: GivenReference }
      | { readonly oneOf: readonly GivenReference[] };
  }[];
}

/**
 * A handler bound to state: in the reactive tier, or at a `bind` site of a
 * body (section 3.14). The handler is a body of this plan, or a handler
 * factory received as a value (section 3.21). A factory value is named by
 * its `identity` slot or, where it reached the binding body in a value the
 * instance computed, by its `identity` entry of that body's `computed`.
 * By ruling the record names no position at which a link to the stream
 * is stored: value code places the stream (below, "Where the stream of a
 * binding is stored").
 */
export interface Binding {
  readonly handler:
    | { readonly body: Index }
    | { readonly factory: GivenReference };
  /** For a factory value, declared by the factory's type. */
  readonly eventSchema: Hash;
  readonly stateSchema: Hash;
  /**
   * What is bound to each path of the handler's state. A binding of the
   * reactive tier has no path with `capture: "copy"`.
   */
  readonly state: readonly {
    readonly path: Path;
    readonly template: Template;
    /**
     * `link`: the path is bound by reference. It holds a cell handle, or a
     * container that has a stored address. In the reactive tier every path
     * is bound this way, and resolves to what `place` names. `copy`: a
     * scalar, or a container the body computed, stored in
     * the binding's state document. A path that holds a reference on some
     * runs only is `copy`, and the runtime stores a link on the runs on
     * which the value it is handed carries a stored address. No class is
     * recorded for a copied path: the copy holds what the bound handler's
     * slots with root `binding` observe of it (section 3.14).
     */
    readonly capture: "copy" | "link";
    /**
     * For a binding of the reactive tier: what the path resolves to. A
     * slot of the instance, which for the index of the element in the
     * collection of an enclosing element body is the slot of root `index`
     * that names that collection; an output of the instance
     * (`Plan.outputs`); the stream of another binding of the reactive tier
     * (`Plan.bindings`); a constant written at the binding, which the
     * plan holds and nothing stores; or, by ruling, the result of the
     * instance, for a path bound to the name of `[SELF]`. `template` is
     * the label of the same
     * place: the `slot` node, which for a slot of root `index` resolves to
     * the label of that collection's array (section 2.2), the `output`
     * node that names the output, and `const` for a stream, for a
     * constant, and for the
     * result of the instance, which is a reference passed on. A constant
     * is held as its value, whether it is written as a literal or as the
     * name of a module-scope constant, which the compiler evaluates. A
     * path bound to `undefined` has no entry of `state`. Absent for a
     * binding made in a function body, whose state document holds the
     * path (section 3.14).
     */
    readonly place?:
      | { readonly slot: Index }
      | { readonly output: Index; readonly site?: Index }
      | { readonly stream: Index }
      | { readonly constant: unknown }
      | { readonly result: true };
    /**
     * For a binding of a pattern compiled in, at a path whose `place`
     * is a slot of the caller that the call bound a path of the
     * callee's argument to: the default the callee declares for that
     * path, as `ReadInput.default` holds it for a body. Assumed
     * (section 8, question 110).
     */
    readonly default?: unknown;
    /**
     * For a path bound by reference in a function body: the reference the
     * binding holds, or the references it is one of, as
     * `WriteEdge.reference` says of a written path. Each is an `identity`
     * slot, or an `identity` entry of the `computed` of the body whose
     * `bind` site refers to the binding.
     */
    readonly reference?:
      | { readonly passes: GivenReference }
      | { readonly oneOf: readonly GivenReference[] };
  }[];
  /**
   * For a binding in the reactive tier: the cause of its stream, with
   * `within`. For a binding made in a function body, `within` is where the
   * `bind` site's body sits, and it does not enter the identifier of the
   * stream (section 3.14).
   */
  readonly name?: Name;
  readonly within: readonly WithinStep[];
}

export interface Plan {
  readonly version: 1;
  /**
   * The identity of each pattern whose source the plan holds code of
   * (section 1.5). Entry 0 is the pattern the plan is compiled from. The
   * others are the patterns compiled into it under a `site` step, each
   * once, in the order of their first site in source.
   */
  readonly patterns: readonly Hash[];
  readonly argumentSchema: Hash;
  readonly resultSchema: Hash;
  readonly slots: readonly Slot[];
  readonly selectors: readonly Selector[];
  readonly picks: readonly Pick[];
  /**
   * The template table. Provisional (P6): every template of the plan
   * that is larger than one leaf node and stands at more than one
   * position, each once, in the order section 3.2 gives ("A template
   * written once"). A `shared` node names an entry by its index. An
   * entry holds `shared` and `output` nodes as any template does, and
   * no two entries are equal.
   */
  readonly templates: readonly Template[];
  readonly collections: readonly Collection[];
  readonly bodies: readonly Body[];
  readonly dynamicReads: readonly DynamicReads[];
  readonly constraints: readonly Constraint[];
  readonly outputs: readonly Output[];
  readonly cones: readonly Cone[];
  readonly edges: readonly ConeEdge[];
  readonly stateCells: readonly StateCell[];
  readonly operations: readonly Operation[];
  readonly children: readonly Child[];
  readonly closures: readonly Closure[];
  readonly bindings: readonly Binding[];
  /**
   * Provisional (P18). The calls, written in this pattern body, of a
   * pattern that is compiled in: a call in the reactive tier and a JSX
   * tag that names a pattern the compiler can see. In source order.
   */
  readonly sites: readonly CallSite[];
  /**
   * Provisional (P18). The record of each pattern that is compiled into
   * the plan, each once, whatever the number of its call sites and
   * whichever record holds them: in the order of `patterns`, entry `i`
   * for the pattern `patterns[i + 1]`.
   */
  readonly callees: readonly Callee[];
}

/**
 * Provisional (P18). The records of one pattern that is compiled into a
 * plan: every list of a `Plan` that holds what a pattern body declares,
 * for the body of that pattern. An `Index` in an entry of these lists
 * indexes the list of the same record, except `CallSite.callee` and
 * `Callee.pattern`, which index lists of the plan. A slot of root
 * `argument` is a path of this pattern's argument. A kept output is one
 * that the result of this pattern reaches, with its path in that result.
 */
export interface Callee extends
  Omit<
    Plan,
    "version" | "patterns" | "argumentSchema" | "resultSchema" | "callees"
  > {
  /** The pattern (`Plan.patterns`). */
  readonly pattern: Index;
}

/**
 * Provisional (P18). One call of a pattern that is compiled in. The
 * record binds the argument of the callee to places of the record that
 * holds the site, and says where that record holds the callee's result.
 */
export interface CallSite {
  /** The callee (`Plan.callees`). */
  readonly callee: Index;
  /** The name of the call: what the `site` step of the call holds. */
  readonly name: Name;
  /**
   * The element bodies of this record that the call is written in, as
   * `element` steps, outermost first. The cones of the callee have an
   * instance for each combination of the keys of these collections, of
   * the collections of the sites that enclose this record, and of the
   * `element` steps of their own `within`.
   */
  readonly within: readonly WithinStep[];
  /** `asScope` on the call (section 8, question 161). */
  readonly scope?: "space" | "user" | "session";
  /** What the call writes at each path of the callee's argument. */
  readonly argument: readonly SiteArgument[];
  /** Where the record that holds the site has the callee's result. */
  readonly result: readonly SiteResult[];
}

/** Provisional (P18). One path of a callee's argument, as a call binds it. */
export interface SiteArgument {
  /** The path of the callee's argument that the call writes. */
  readonly path: Path;
  /**
   * What the call wrote there, in the record that holds the site: a
   * slot, an output, the stream of a binding, a constant, or the result
   * of the instance, as `Binding.state` has them for a path of a
   * handler's state. A slot of root `argument` there is bound in turn by
   * the site that calls that record. That the last two forms are needed
   * is assumed (section 8, question 170).
   */
  readonly place:
    | { readonly slot: Index }
    | { readonly output: Index; readonly site?: Index }
    | { readonly stream: Index }
    | { readonly constant: unknown }
    | { readonly result: true };
  /**
   * For a `place` that is a slot of root `argument` of the record that
   * holds the site: the default which the pattern of that record
   * declares for that path of its own argument, where it declares one.
   * It is the default of a place on the chain of a read (section 2.5).
   */
  readonly default?: unknown;
  /**
   * The key fields that the type of the place, or of the argument
   * expression, declares for an array at this path, where a construct
   * of the callee iterates it (`Collection.keyFields`).
   */
  readonly keyFields?: readonly string[];
}

/** Provisional (P18). One place that holds a callee's result. */
export interface SiteResult {
  /** A path of what the callee returns: `["$UI"]` at a child position. */
  readonly from: Path;
  /**
   * The path, in the result of the record that holds the site, at which
   * the value at `from` stands, with `*` for each element step of
   * `CallSite.within`.
   */
  readonly at: Path;
}

/** What the compiler emits, addressed as one thing. */
export interface CompiledPattern {
  readonly plan: Hash;
  readonly valueCode: Hash;
  /**
   * Content address of the compiler build that produced both. A
   * deployment accepts a stated set of builds (section 7.2).
   */
  readonly compiler: Hash;
}
```

The **keep set** is the outputs with `kept: true`. The rendered tree under
`[UI]` is part of the result and is kept, so a value bound into it is a kept
output. The saving for such a value is that it is a path of the result with
a memoized label, written in the transaction that computed it, and not a
node with a document and a transaction of its own. The keep set is stored in
as many documents as serve its readers, and section 2.3 says what a split
has to preserve.

The keep set is a property of the pattern and not of a run: the compiler
knows which output paths the result cell's schema reaches.

A pattern compiled into another has no plan of its own: a `map` body, an
inline sub-pattern, and a call in the reactive tier of a pattern the compiler
can see. Its slots, bodies and cones are entries of the enclosing plan, with
`element` roots where it reads the element. A pattern the compiler cannot
see at the call, and any pattern a function body instantiates, is a `Child`
with a plan of its own (section 3.15). That sentence, and what this
document says of the entries of a pattern compiled in, is about the
written-out form of a plan. Provisional (P18): a plan holds a pattern
that a call or a tag names once, as a record that its call sites name
("A pattern compiled in is written once", below).

A JSX tag that names a pattern is such a call: `<Row message={m} />` is
`Row({ message: m })` (`language-subset.md` §4.5). Where the tag names a
pattern the compiler can see, the pattern is compiled into the enclosing plan under a
`site` step whose name is the tag's name, and its attributes are the paths of
its argument, bound place by place as below. The children written between the
tags are the path `children` of the argument, an array literal of the
children, as the JSX factory passes them (`h` in
`runtime/runner/src/builder/h.ts`). The tag evaluates to what the pattern
returns, as the call does. *Assumed,* with question 53 of section 8: the
entries of the enclosing rendered tree at the tag's position are those of the
callee's `[UI]`, since that is what a renderer shows of a result at a child
position. That is a rule about the position and not about the tag: it holds
for a tag, for a call, and for a variable that holds the result of either,
wherever one is written at a child position of a view node. At every other
place, such as a path of the result, a path of an argument, or the value of
an attribute, the tag evaluates to the callee's result, and the entries at
that place are those of the result, with the callee's tree below `$UI`: for
`controls: <Controls />` in a returned record the callee's tree is at
`controls/$UI`. Where the tag names a factory value, the instantiation is a
`Child` with one write edge of target `argument` per attribute and one at
`children`. Its callee is `{ factory }` with the `identity` slot of the
factory value. A factory value that the instance itself computed in the
reactive tier has no such slot and no body to name an entry of; *assumed*
(section 8, question 58):
the tag is refused there, and the author passes the factory value in the
argument or instantiates it in a function body. A pattern is one the compiler
can see whichever module declares it and however that module exports it, a
default export included.

The argument of a pattern compiled into another is bound place by place.
Each path of the callee's argument resolves to what the caller wrote
there: a slot of the caller, an output of the caller, or a constant. So a
slot the callee reads through its argument is a slot of the enclosing
plan with the caller's root and path, and no slot with root `argument`
stands for the callee's own argument. A call of a statically resolved
pattern that is on a cycle of such calls, a pattern that calls itself in
its reactive tier included, cannot be compiled in this way, because the
plan would not end. *Assumed* (section 8, question 45): the compiler
refuses such a call.

**A constant of the argument, and a path the call leaves out.** A
constant that the call writes at a path of the callee's argument has no
record. It is in the value code of the cones that read the path, which
the compiler emits for that call. Provisional (P18): the constant is
the `place` of the call's entry of `CallSite.argument`, the runtime
hands it to the cones that read the path, and the value code of the
callee is emitted once. The callee can also declare a default
for a path that the call does not write, as a callee that declares
`symbol: Default<string, "$">` does where the call writes no `symbol`.
A path the call leaves out resolves to no slot, and no record holds the
callee's argument schema, since the callee is no `Child`. By ruling the
compiler writes the callee's declared default into the plan as a
constant for that path: the path is bound as if the call had written,
as a constant, the default that the callee's declared argument type
gives it. It is held as a constant that the call writes is, and it has
no label. In the prototype's comparison the runtime of today, for which
the callee is an instance with an argument document and a schema, read
`"$"` at such a path.

By the same ruling a path that the call binds to a slot of the caller at
which nothing is stored also reads the callee's default, as it does
today. The slot's value is absent, and the cones that read the path
take the callee's default for it, a constant of the value code that the
compiler emits for that call. The read carries the label of the slot,
with the empty integrity that a read of a default has (section 2.5).
Where the place the slot resolves to declares a default of its own, the
rule of section 2.5 ("A default belongs to the place") gives the read
that default. By ruling the default of the place governs there: the
default read at a position is the one declared nearest the end of the
chain of places the read resolves through, and the callee's default is
read only where no place along the chain declares one. So a caller's
argument at which nothing is stored, or a cell the caller bound, that
declares a default wins over the callee's default, as it does in the
runtime of today (section 2.5).

Four things follow from the ruling and the rules above.

- **The one record that shows the default.** The constant of a path the
  call leaves out is in the value code. A handler binding of the callee
  whose state captures the path holds it too, as it holds a constant
  the call writes: for a callee that declares
  `step: Default<number, 5>` and binds a handler over `step`, the
  entry of `Binding.state` has the `place` `{ constant: 5 }`.
- **How the callee names the path does not matter.** The default is
  that of the path of the callee's declared argument type. It is read
  where the callee destructures its parameter and where it reads a
  member of a parameter it does not destructure, as `props.symbol`.
- **A call that passes one value for the whole argument** writes no
  path of it. Each path of the callee's argument then resolves to a
  path below what the caller passed. Below a slot the second half of
  the ruling applies. Below an output of the caller that holds nothing
  at the path, the callee's default is read by the ruling on the order
  of defaults: the callee is the reader, and no place along the chain
  declares a default.
- **Nothing stored means absent.** A stored `null` is a value, and no
  default is read in its place. A stored `undefined` is assumed to
  read as absent does (section 2.5; section 8, question 104).

Two further rulings say how the callee's default reaches what is not
a read of a cone. Both are the same where the callee is called in an
element body, over an array of references, over an array of plain
values in place, and over the result of another per-element construct.

- **A sandboxed body of the callee finds the default in the plan.** A
  body of the callee that reads a path bound to a slot at which nothing
  is stored has to find the callee's default in its argument. By ruling
  the entry of `Body.reads` holds it: `ReadInput.default` is the
  default the callee declares for the path, and value code does not
  pass it. The runtime puts the default at the entry's place where the
  slot yields nothing and no place the slot resolves through declares
  a default of its own (`execution-and-storage.md` §2.2). A `Body` has
  the `site` step of the call in its `within`, so two calls of one
  callee have two records, and each holds the default of its own call.
  Provisional (P18): the body is one record of the callee, its entry
  holds the callee's own default, and the default of an outer callee
  is in the entry of `CallSite.argument` that binds the path ("A
  pattern compiled in is written once", below).
  Where a callee calls another pattern that is compiled in, and both
  calls bind one slot of the outermost caller, the entry of a body of
  the inner callee holds the default of the outer callee where that
  declares one, and the inner callee's own otherwise. That follows
  from the ruling on the order of defaults: the outer callee's place
  is nearer the end of the chain that the read resolves through, and
  the reader's own default is read only where no place along the
  chain declares one.
  A handler is one `Body` however many bindings name it, and which path
  of the callee's argument a state path of it is bound to is a fact of
  the binding. *Assumed* (section 8, question 110): for a state path of
  a binding whose `place` is such a slot, the entry of `Binding.state`
  holds the default, in a member `default`, and the runtime applies it
  when it resolves the path at dispatch.
- **A callee that passes the path on by reference** reads nothing of
  it. Where a path of the callee's result passes on such a path of its
  argument, and the path is bound to a slot of the caller at which
  nothing is stored, the result holds a link to the caller's slot. By
  ruling the stored reference carries the callee's declared default:
  the link holds the schema that the callee declares for the path, and
  so its default, as every link holds the schema of the place it names
  as the plan that wrote the link declares it (section 2.5). A reader
  of that path of the result resolves the link. The link is on the
  chain of the read and the caller's place ends it, so the reader reads
  the default of the caller's place where that declares one, and the
  callee's default otherwise. That is the value the runtime of today
  shows, for which the callee is an instance with an argument schema.
  The read has the empty integrity of a default either way. *Assumed*
  (section 8, question 110): the rule holds for every reference to a
  path of its argument that code of the callee stores, in a state
  cell, in the argument of a child, or through a handle, as it does
  for one at a path of the result.

No record of the plan holds what such a reference carries. A slot has
the schema of its reader, and the place the caller bound has the
caller's schema, so the schema that the callee declares for the path,
and with it the default, is in no record that the runtime reads when
it stores the link. And where code of the caller names a path of the
callee's result that passes the argument path on, as `price.symbol`
does for a callee that returns its `symbol`, the compiler resolves
the name to the caller's slot at compile time, and no link is stored
for that read at all. *Assumed* (section 8, question 119): value code
supplies the default. Where value code of the callee stores the
reference, it hands the runtime the reference together with the
callee's default, and the runtime stores the link with that default
in its schema unless the schema of the caller's place declares one.
Where code of the caller reads such a path of the result, the
compiler writes a read of the slot that takes the callee's default
where the slot yields nothing, as expression code of the callee
does. The prototype does the first and not the second, which is a
defect of it. Both are the same in an element body over an array of
references, over an array of plain values in place, and over the
result of another per-element construct.

**A pattern compiled in is written once.** Provisional (P18; section 8, question
170). The paragraphs above, and every rule of this document that speaks of "the
enclosing plan", describe a plan in which a pattern that is compiled in is
written out at each call: its slots, bodies, cones, outputs, edges and templates
stand among those of the caller once per call, with a `site` step in each
`within`. This document calls that the **written-out form**. With a callee that
is called at two sites and that calls another pattern at two sites in turn, the
written-out form holds four copies of the innermost, and `D` such levels hold 2
to the power `D`. The prototype measured it: 3,193, 7,746, 16,961, 35,665,
73,936 and 152,575 bytes of plan, and 5, 13, 29, 61, 125 and 253 cones, for 1 to
6 levels, where the source grows by 148 bytes for each level. The template table
shares nothing between the copies, because their slot indexes differ.

A plan therefore does not hold the written-out form. It holds each pattern that
is compiled in once, as a **callee record** (`Plan.callees`), and each call as a
**call-site record** (`sites` of the record whose pattern body the call is
written in). The written-out form stays the definition of what a plan means: the
labels, the values, the causal identifiers and the stored documents of an
instance are those that the rules of this document give for the written-out form
of its plan. The rest of this paragraph says how each record of that form is
found from the two kinds of record, and which rules are evaluated once for a
callee and which once for a site.

*Which patterns have a callee record.* Every pattern that a call in the reactive
tier or a JSX tag names and that the compiler can see, the one that is called at
a single site included, so the compiler has no choice in it. The callback of an
element construct and an inline pattern are written at one place, and stay
entries of the record of the pattern body they are written in. A pattern has one
callee record in a plan, whichever records hold its sites: the caller of a
callee can be the pattern the plan is compiled from or another callee. The
refusal of a cycle of such calls stands (question 45), so the callee records of
a plan form no cycle.

*The callee record.* A `Callee` has the lists that a `Plan` has for what a
pattern body declares: `slots`, `selectors`, `picks`, `templates`,
`collections`, `bodies`, `dynamicReads`, `constraints`, `outputs`, `cones`,
`edges`, `stateCells`, `operations`, `children`, `closures`, `bindings` and
`sites`. Each is formed by the rules of this document for a pattern body,
applied to the body of the callee alone, as they would be applied if the callee
had a plan of its own. Five things differ from an entry of the written-out form.

- An `Index` indexes the list of the callee record. No entry of a callee names
  an entry of a caller.
- A path of the callee's argument is a slot of root `argument` with that path,
  where the written-out form has the caller's slot or output. The sentence
  above, that no slot with root `argument` stands for the callee's own argument,
  holds for the written-out form and not for a callee record.
- A `within` holds the `element` steps of the callee's own body and no `site`
  step.
- `Output.kept` and `Output.path` are relative to what the callee returns: an
  output is kept where the callee's result reaches it, and its path is the path
  in that result.
- A member `pattern` of a `derive` or a `fold` is absent, because all code of a
  callee record is written in the one pattern that `Callee.pattern` names. The
  atom of the pattern (section 3.2) is that pattern's.

A callee record depends on nothing of its call sites. What the written-out form
takes from a call is held by the call-site record: the binding of the argument,
the constants that the call writes, the key fields that the caller's types
declare for an array which the callee iterates, the defaults of the places along
the chain of a read, the scope of an `asScope` modifier, and the places of the
result.

*The call-site record.* A `CallSite` names its callee and has five further
members.

- `name` is the name of the call by the rules of section 1.3: it is what the
  `site` step of the written-out form holds.
- `within` has the `element` steps of the element bodies, of the record that
  holds the site, that the call is written in.
- `scope` is the scope of an `asScope` modifier on the call.
- `argument` has an entry for each path of the callee's argument that the call
  writes, as the source writes it: one entry for each property of an argument
  object and each attribute of a tag, one at `children` for the children of a
  tag, and one entry with the empty path for a call that passes one value for
  the whole argument. A member of a nested object literal that the call writes
  is an entry at the longer path. The entry's `place` is what the call wrote, in
  the record that holds the site: a slot, an output, a constant, and, *assumed,*
  the stream of a binding or the result of the instance, the five forms that
  `Binding.state` has for a path of a handler's state. A path that the call
  leaves out has no entry.
- `result` has an entry for each place at which the record that holds the site
  has what the callee returns: `from` is a path of the callee's result and `at`
  the path in the result of the holding record. A tag, a call, or a variable
  that holds the result of either, written at a child position of a view node,
  is an entry with `from` equal to `$UI` and `at` the position, which is the
  rule for a tag above. At every other place of the result, `from` is the path
  that the caller wrote, the empty path for the whole result.

*Indexes.* Every index is scoped to one record: the plan's own lists for the
pattern the plan is compiled from, and the lists of one callee. Three members
cross a record. `CallSite.callee` and `Callee.pattern` index `Plan.callees` and
`Plan.patterns`. A member that names an output with `site` names an entry of the
`outputs` of the callee of that site, which is how a record names what a callee
returns. And a `place` of `CallSite.argument` names an entry of the record that
holds the site, which is how a callee is given what its caller has. Nothing else
crosses: a caller names no slot, cone, body, selector, state cell or template of
a callee, and a callee names nothing of a caller. Where this or another document
writes `Plan.slots`, `Plan.outputs` or another list for what an index names, it
is the list of the record that holds the index.

*A slot of root `argument` at a site.* For the cone instances of one site, a
slot of root `argument` with path `p` of the callee is bound through the entries
of `CallSite.argument`:
