query. *Assumed:* it is written in the reactive tier alone.
`language-subset.md` §4.4 lists it among the calls of tier R and its §5.2
refuses it in a function body (`function-body:wish`), the corpus has no
call in a function body (`builtin-inventory.md`, "Calls inside function
bodies"), and `Body.calls` has no site for one.

- **The operation.** An `Operation` of kind `wish`, with
  `implementation: { builtin: "wish" }`, named by `name` and `within` as
  any operation is (section 1.3).
- **The operands.** The cone the call is written in computes the operands
  the author wrote, among `query`, `path`, `schema`, `scope`, `context`
  and `headless`, and writes each into the operation's state by a
  `WriteEdge` with target `request`, at the path of the operand's name,
  with the template of its expression. An operand that is a container or
  a cell is held by reference, as in any request. `Operation.input` is
  the join of those templates, and it is `const` for a call whose
  operands are all constants.
  - The argument is a record of type `WishParams` (`WishFunction` in
    `base/api/index.ts`). A string written as the argument is no value
    of that type and is refused by the type check
    (`subset-type:mismatch`), and so is a member the type does not
    declare.
  - Each operand is one edge, at the path of its name and no deeper. For
    an operand that is a record or an array written in place, the
    edge's template is the template of the value observed whole
    (section 3.4): the join of the templates of its entries.
  - Where the argument is written with a spread, its members are those
    section 3.4 gives the object literal. A member the spread's type
    declares as optional has the `select` of that rule as its template.
- **The result.** The stored result of the operation has the paths of
  `WishState` (`base/api/index.ts`): `result`, `candidates`, `error`,
  `errorCode` and `[UI]`. A reader has slots with root `operation` at the
  paths it reads, and its template has the `slot` nodes. `result` and
  each member of `candidates` hold a reference to what was found, and a
  slot whose path continues below one crosses that link (section 2.5), so
  the content has its own label.
- **What the runtime does.** The built-in resolves the target in the
  transaction that evaluates a reader of the result, and in a
  transaction of the cause that changed something it read. It has no
  request transaction, stages nothing that leaves the runtime, and no
  egress ceiling is checked. What it creates, it creates under an
  identifier derived from the operation's cause, so a second resolution
  creates nothing.
- **Its reads.** The plan has one entry of `Plan.dynamicReads` of kind
  `search` that names the operation. It stands for the reads the
  resolution made of what no slot names: the links it followed along a
  path, the tests of whether a target holds anything, and the name and
  the schema of every candidate a search considered, whether or not the
  candidate matched. They are journaled with their trigger reads, as a
  followed link is (section 3.10).

The label rule has one form for every query.

```text
C(a path of the result) = C(Operation.input) ⊔ C(dynamic, kind search)
I(a path of the result) = empty
```

No integrity is minted, as today. The same label is the identity label of
the reference at `result` and at each member of `candidates`: which
target was found depends on the operands and on what the resolution read.

The rule is how the runtime resolves a slot, and no node of a reader's
template states it. A reader's template has the `slot` node with root
`operation` and nothing else for the read: no `dynamic` node, and no
copy of `Operation.input`. When the runtime resolves a slot whose root
is an operation of kind `wish`, the label is the instantiated
`Operation.input` of that operation joined with the label of the entry
of `Plan.dynamicReads` of kind `search` that names it. The two parts are
in the plan, and the join is made at resolution (section 4.2), as the
label of any slot with root `operation` comes from the operation's
record.
The rest of the operation's state document has the label section 2.6
gives the bookkeeping of an operation.

**The outcome of each `wish` has a label of its own.** An evaluation can
resolve several operations of kind `wish` in one transaction: the wishes
of one instance are resolved together when a reader of each is evaluated.
The label stored at the paths of one outcome is the label of that
operation alone, its `Operation.input` joined with the reads of its own
entry of `Plan.dynamicReads`. It is not the join of the transaction, which
holds the operands and the reads of every wish the transaction resolved,
so the name a pattern reads through `#profileName` does not take the label
of the candidates a search by hashtag considered in the same transaction.
The reads of a resolution are therefore attributed to the operation that
made them, as the reads through a handle are attributed to their `dynamic`
node (section 3.10), and the write of an outcome is a write that a record
of the plan covers: the runtime has, for each outcome the transaction
writes, the operation, the bindings of the slots that `Operation.input`
reaches, and the addresses its resolution read. The record names the operation,
and the runtime gives the write the label of the rule above, with no integrity.
Where a record reports no reads for the entry of `Plan.dynamicReads`, that part
is the transaction's join, which is a bound. A read of the outcome in the
transaction that wrote it takes the label staged for the outcome, also at a path
below it (section 4.5). Whether a `wish` failed is decided by its resolution, as
its outcome is: a slot that reads the mark of a failure, which the operation's
state does not hold, is bound to the outcome and has its label. Milestone 4 of
the integration builds the record
([compiled-pattern-language-integration.md](../../plans/compiled-pattern-language-integration.md)):
`wishOutcomeLabel` in `runtime/runner/src/cfc/plan-labels.ts`.

The query decides what the `dynamic` node can hold, the scope, and which
other records the plan has. Where the `query` operand is a constant, the
compiler reads its key, the first segment as `parseWishTarget`
(`runtime/runner/src/builtins/wish.ts`) splits it, and the plan has the
row of that key.

| The constant query | Part | What the plan has beside the operation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/`, `/a/b`, or a path below `#default`, `#mentionable`, `#summaryIndex`, `#knowledgeGraph`, `#pieceRegistry` | A path or a well-known target of the current space | Nothing. The `dynamic` node holds the links followed along the path |
| `#favorites`, `#journal`, `#learned`, `#learnedSummary`, `#agent_queue`, `#chatManager`, `#profile`, `#profileName`, `#profileBio`, `#profileSpace`, with or without a path | A well-known target of the home space of the demanding principal | `Operation.scope` is `user`. For a profile target without `headless: true`, a `Child` for each of the two profile sidecars (below) |
| `#now` with no path | The one-shot clock | A `StateCell` of scope `space`, named from the operation's `name` with the suffix `/now`, with the operation's `within`. The runtime writes the coarsened time into it once, when it is empty, and `result` is a reference to it. The cell has no input label. The `dynamic` node holds nothing |
| `#now/N` | The ticking clock, `N` whole seconds | Nothing. `result` is a reference to the clock cell of the space for that interval, which the runtime writes. The cell has no input label. Each tick is a commit of the runtime's, and it reaches a reader in a set of changes, as any change from storage does (Notation). The `dynamic` node holds nothing |
| Any other `#tag` | A search by hashtag | `Operation.scope` is `user` unless the `scope` operand is a constant that names neither `"~"` nor `"profile"` (`wishTargetMayUseHomeSpace`). Without `headless: true`, a `Child` for the suggestion sidecar. The `dynamic` node holds the name and schema of every candidate considered |
| `#profilePicture`, `#profileAvatar`, `#profile/picture`, `#profile/avatar` | None: the target is refused | Nothing. The result holds the error, with the label of `Operation.input` |
| Any other string | A suggestion for the situation the query describes | `Operation.scope` is `user`. Without `headless: true`, a `Child` for the suggestion sidecar. With it the result holds nothing and no instance is made |

A `path` operand is appended to the path the query names. It may be
computed, except in two cases, where the compiler emits the records of
every row the path could select.

- With the key `#now` the path decides between the two clocks, so a
  computed `path` keeps the `StateCell` of the one-shot clock.
- With the key `#profile` the path decides between a home target and
  the refused targets `#profile/picture` and `#profile/avatar`, so a
  computed `path` has the row of the home target.

**What counts as a constant.** The `query`, `path`, `scope` and
`headless` operands are constants where each is a literal written at
the call, or a name that resolves to a module-scope constant with a
static initializer (`language-subset.md` §8.8), whose value the compiler
reads. A constant `path` is an array literal whose members are
constants. `headless` is `true` for the table only where it is the
constant `true`. An operand that is anything else is computed, and the
compiler emits the records of every row it could select. Treating a
constant as computed adds records and removes none, so it is sound and
costs the records. `wish:computed-query` is reported at the call, once,
for a `query` that is computed, and for a `path` that is computed where
the constant query is exactly `#now` or `#profile`.

**A sidecar** is a `Child` whose callee is one of three system patterns,
`{ compiled }` with that pattern's content address: the suggestion
pattern, the profile-creation pattern, and the profile picker
(`launchSuggestionPattern`, `launchProfileCreatePattern` and
`launchProfilePickerPattern` in `wish.ts`). The sidecars' names are
`suggestion`, `profileCreate` and `profilePicker`. The `name` of the
`Child` is the record of the operation's `name` and the sidecar's name
(`Name`, section 1.1), with the operation's `within`, so its
identifier derives from the wish's cause. The built-in instantiates it on
the runs that need it, writes its argument under the label of the result,
and stores a link to its result at `[UI]`, or at `result` for a
suggestion. The instance belongs to the operation: a resolution that no
longer needs it tears it down, as a computation's instance is (section
3.14).

**A query that is not a constant.** The record is the same operation with
the same label rule, since the `dynamic` node holds whatever the
resolution read. The compiler cannot leave anything out: `Operation.scope`
is `user`, the plan has the `StateCell` of the one-shot clock and a
`Child` for each of the three sidecars, and a tick of a clock can make a
reader stale.
*Assumed,* with `builtin-inventory.md` (its open question 2; section 8,
question 48): such a call compiles, with a hint that names the cost
(`wish:computed-query`, `language-subset.md` §10.2).

**Today.** The result is a reference, the action's transaction joins the
operands and every read the resolution made, and hashtag search joins
every candidate it reads (`resolveBase` and `searchByHashtag` in
`runtime/runner/src/builtins/wish.ts`). **Equal.** The 50 ms debounce has
no counterpart (`builtin-inventory.md`, "Effectful built-ins"). *Assumed*
(section 8, question 47): the record above, an operation of a kind of its
own.

### 3.21 A handler factory received as a value

A handler can be passed by reference and bound where it arrives: in the
reactive tier, or at a `bind` site of a body. The compiler then knows the
handler's type and not the handler. This parallels the child instance of
section 3.15.

**What the enclosing plan records** (`Binding` with `handler.factory`): the
slot that holds the factory, observed for `identity`, or the entry of
`Body.computed` that holds it (below); the event and state
schemas the factory's type declares; and, for each state path, the template
of what is bound to it and whether it is copied or bound by reference. The
rule of section 3.14 decides that from the value the binder has at the
path and not from the handler, so it needs no knowledge of the handler.

**What the handler's own record supplies.** A handler factory value names a
compiled handler by content address. The compiled module it comes from
holds the handler's `Body` record, and the runtime resolves it when the
binding is made:

- the **footprint**: which state and event paths the body reads, and the
  handles it reads through. The runtime narrows the argument to it, as for
  any body. The declared state schema bounds what the binder passes; the
  footprint can only be narrower.
- the **write edges**: the paths the body writes, relative to the cells in
  its state, with their constraints, and its `outputs` and `calls`.
- the **body identity**, `Body.code`, which is what a `WriterPolicy.body`
  names and what `TransformedBy` carries.

**Labels.** The handler's template, when an event arrives, is its own
record's `derive` over its event and `binding` slots, joined with the
`identity` slot of the factory: which handler runs is a function of that
slot, so its label is on everything the handler writes. The stream's
identity derives from the enclosing instance, the factory's content address
and what the binding holds (section 3.14). Which stream exists therefore
reveals which handler arrived, so the stream's identity label is the join
of the templates of the state paths and the label of the factory's
`identity` slot.

**A factory bound in a function body.** At a `bind` site,
`handler.factory` names the `identity` slot the body has at the factory's
position. For a factory that reached the body in a value the instance
computed, it names the factory's `identity` entry of that body's
`computed` (`GivenReference`), and the entry's template takes the place of
the slot's label in the identity label of the stream.

Which handler such a binding holds is fixed when the binding is made. The
stream's identifier holds the factory's content address, so another
factory at the same place is another stream. The label of which handler
it is is fixed with it. *Assumed:* the transaction that makes the binding
instantiates the label of the factory's `identity` slot, or the template
of its entry, and stores it in the binding's state document with the
factory's content address, as it stores the label of a copied path. When
an event arrives, the handler's template joins the label stored there,
where the rule above has the label of the slot. Two things make the
stored label necessary. An entry of `Body.computed` has no address at
which a label could be resolved when an event arrives. And a slot of the
binding body can have a root that is bound only while that body runs,
such as the event of the handler that made the binding. For a binding of
the reactive tier the factory's slot is a slot of the instance, and its
label is resolved when the event arrives.

**Checks that move from compile time to run time.**

| Check | With a known handler | With a factory value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The writer policy of a written path names this handler | Compile time, for a static write edge (section 4.4) | When the handler writes: the resolved `Body.code` against the policy of the cell it was bound to |
| The handler's schemas fit the binding | Compile time | When the binding is made: the resolved record's event and state schemas against the declared ones. A misfit fails the binding's cone, or the binding handler |
| Input requirements and ceilings on the handler's state | Compile time where the bound slots are declared | At instantiation, from the resolved record's constraints over the `binding` slots |
| Some element of the pattern binds the handler under the surface its UI contract names | Compile time, reported as a warning (section 4.4) | Not checkable; per event only |
| A write the handler's record does not list | Compile time | Refused by the runtime when attempted (section 7.3) |

**What is hard.**

- **The write surface of a pattern is no longer closed at compile time.** A
  cell passed as state to a handler value can be written by code the
  compiler never saw. Every analysis that asks "who writes this cell" has
  to count such a cell as written by an unknown handler: the detection of
  cycles through side-writes, and any classification of a cell as written
  only by computations.
- **The static error becomes a run-time refusal.** Passing the wrong
  handler to a cell whose policy names another is found when the handler
  first writes, not when the pattern is compiled.
- **The record has to be available where the binding runs.** A client that
  speculates the handler needs the handler's compiled module, which the
  binder's compiled pattern does not contain. It is fetched by content
  address, like a child's plan.
- **A handler's policy names it by type.** A type such as the one a write
  policy uses names a handler definition. A handler value satisfies it only
  if it *is* that definition, which the content address decides at run
  time; the type checker of the binder can check the declared schemas and
  nothing more.

**Today.** A handler factory read from a cell is plain data and cannot be
bound (`builtin-inventory.md`, "Factory values"). This is new, so there is
nothing to compare.

### 3.22 Summary

| Operation | Template | Against today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Property access | Slot path extension | Equal |
| Object, array construction | Template per path | Equal in pattern bodies; tighter in promoted expressions |
| Conditional | `select` | Equal to the `derived` part; tighter than the static part of section 3.1, by ruling, with the static part included in the comparison (question 69): today a conditional over references stores no label of its condition, a finding against the runtime (section 3.5). A promoted `computed` mints no atom for its callback's code, by ruling; a conditional in one that is a kept output carries the pattern's atom, which the comparison takes as corresponding to the callback's |
| A kept output (section 3.2) | The output's template, with the `TransformedBy` atom of the instance's pattern added; in the label of the content at the output path where the output passes a value on by reference | Tighter on integrity, by ruling: an atom where the runtime stores none for a value the pattern body passes on or an unlabeled value; for a promoted `computed`, an atom that names the pattern where the runtime's names the callback |
| `map` | Element template; membership slot | Equal to the `derived` part; the container tighter than the static part of section 3.1, by ruling; tighter within an element as above |
| `filter` | Pass-through elements; membership `fold` of predicates | Equal |
| `flatMap` | Element template; membership `fold` of segment lengths | Tighter (content of other segments excluded) |
| `count`, `sum`, `min`, `max` | `fold` | Equal; `count` equal or tighter |
| `minBy`, `maxBy` | `pick`, choice a `fold` of the key function | Equal |
| `findIndex`, `some`, `every` | `fold` through the deciding element | Tighter (later elements excluded) |
| `find` | `pick`, choice a prefix `fold` | Tighter (later elements excluded) |
| `reduce` | `fold` of the step expression, plus the initial value | Equal; tighter when the expression selects |
| `groupBy`, `keyBy`, `lookup`, `keys`, `keyEntries` | Bucket membership a `fold` of the key function; `pick` for `key` mode | **Looser**, the first exception: absent elements' keys are included |
| Dynamic key `a[k]` | `pick` over a container | Equal |
| Template literal | `derive` over substitutions | Equal; tighter inside a constructed object |
| Sandboxed call | `derive` over slots, computed inputs and handles; references passed through | Equal or tighter; **looser**, the second exception, for a static read through a handle on a run that throws before it |
| Link following | A slot whose path crosses the link; `identity` slot plus `dynamic` where the path is not named | Equal |
| Static side-write | Template of the written expression | Equal or tighter |
| Write through a handle bound to a value the instance computes | None where the path holds a produced value: the write is refused. Template of the written expression where the path holds a reference, and the write lands at the reference's target | Equal for a reference; a refused write changes no label |
| A slot that reads as a default (section 2.5) | The slot's confidentiality; the empty integrity | **Looser** on integrity, the third exception, by ruling. A slot that reads a stored object whole is equal |
| Write through a resolved reference | Template of the written expression, which holds the links the resolution follows; lands where the resolution ends | Equal |
| Materializer | Today's join on every path it writes, its result included | Equal |
| Handler | `derive` over event and state footprint | Equal or tighter (an authored event type is read whole today); the second exception applies |
| Calls in a body | The body's template on what it creates; the egress ceiling on a request and the content it holds by reference, sent or only hashed, and on each later send | Equal; tighter for references a re-evaluated body passes on. The check on a later send is new |
| Instance made by a `lift` or a `computed` | The body's template on the argument, written by each evaluation; the instance named by the site and an ordinal, or by an explicit cause | Equal |
| Handler binding | Nothing copied in the reactive tier; in a body, a scalar and a computed container copied with the body's template, a handle and a stored container bound by reference | Equal or tighter: the body that makes the binding does not read a container it binds by reference |
| Child instance | Argument templates in; `child` slots out | Equal |
| Pattern closure | Join of the capture templates on the factory value; `params` slots inside | Equal |
| Pattern closure given to a language model as a tool | The label of the model's output on the argument and on the existence of the instance; the instance's own result labels on the result | New |
| What an element body stores per element key (section 2.6) | The template of what is stored, instantiated for the key at the one position that holds it | Equal: today each occurrence of an element has a run of its own |
| Handler factory value | The handler's own record, plus the factory's `identity` | New |
| Context reads | `cause`, `labelMetadata`, `identity` slots; `dynamic` for access lists and journaled observations | Equal |
| `anchorsOf`, `cellFromUrl` parsing, `wish` | References with computed identity; for `wish`, an operation whose result joins its operands and a `dynamic` node of kind `search` | Equal |
| Stored state that is not an output (section 2.6) | The operation's input, the cone-level join, or the output's label | New |

Three things are looser, and all three are decided: the collection index, a
slot for a read through a handle on a run that throws before the read, and the
integrity of a slot that reads as a default (section 3.1). A promoted
`computed` is not a fourth: by ruling it mints no `TransformedBy` atom for the
code of its callback, and its kept outputs carry the atom of the pattern
(section 3.2). Under the assumption of question 71 of section 8, a value that
a promoted `computed` passes on unchanged to the argument of a child, the
target of a write edge, or the request of an effect has no atom where today
it has the callback's. Another way a compiled label could be
looser than today's is a static footprint standing in for reads that are
dynamic today, and `handles` exclude it: a read a body makes through a cell
on some runs only, or at a path it computes, stays journaled. A widening
that covers data slots affects only what the runtime materializes into the
argument, which the body's argument schema materializes today as well. A
widening on a handle turns its reads into journaled ones under the handle's
declared type, which is what the runtime records for them today. A read
through a handle at a static place that is conditional stays dynamic for the
same reason. A handler binding is not a further one either: a binding made in a
function body copies a scalar and a container the body computed, and binds a
stored container by reference, as the runtime does today (section 3.14).

## 4. Instantiation

### 4.1 When it runs

Instantiation runs in the transaction that evaluated a value, after the
value code, and only for the templates of what the transaction stores or
checks:

- a kept output (`Output.template`);
- a write edge (`WriteEdge.template`): a side-write, a write through a
  handle, a path of a child's argument, the initial value of a created
  cell, a path of an effect's stored request;
- the request of an effect, where the transaction checks the egress
  ceiling: the join of the request's templates and of what its references
  lead to, as far as the effect serializes or hashes them (section 3.14).
  A later send of the effect is checked in a send transaction on the
  labels its reads consume, and no template is instantiated for it;
- a state path that a binding made in a function body stores
  (`Binding.state`): a copied path, which is a scalar or a container the
  body computed, and the link of a path bound by reference, whose pointer
  label is the path's template. Both are stored in the binding's state
  document (section 3.14). For a handler factory value bound in a function
  body, the label of which factory it is is instantiated and stored there
  as well (section 3.21). A binding of the reactive tier has no state
  document, so nothing is instantiated for it;
- a parameter of a pattern closure that is copied (`Closure.params`), which
  is stored with the factory value, or with the instance where the closure
  is the callee of an instantiation in a function body (section 3.15);
- an output a cache stores (section 2.6);
- the other stored state of section 2.6, each under the label its row of
  the table there gives: the bookkeeping of an operation, the other
  members of a cache entry, a provenance record, the origin facts of a
  kept derived collection, the record of the instances a computation
  made, and an allocation record.

This list is the whole of what is instantiated.
`execution-and-storage.md` §1.6 and §1.9 refer to it.

**Only a serving runtime commits labels from templates.** By ruling
(2026-11-19), a label from a template is stored only by a transaction that a
serving runtime commits. A client's speculative run evaluates the same
templates for the gates the client evaluates, and is never the stored
result. The store does not verify a label from a template: it
accepts it from the serving runtime as it accepts that runtime's other
derived labels. An exception for storage held in memory for tests is
allowed only where it makes the whole simpler, and none is built.

For each one:

1. Decide whether there is anything to do. There is when one of these
   holds, and otherwise the step ends:
   - the cone or body that computes it was evaluated in this transaction;
   - something demands it, and a slot its template reaches under its last
     selections has a new label and an unchanged value;
   - it is a kept output, something demands it, and its current value was
     computed in a transaction that did not store it: one that a handler's
     failure aborted, one that a failed constraint rejected, an attempt
     that was withdrawn whole or whose event was queued again (section
     5.4; `scheduler-and-serving-loop.md` §5.5), or one whose commit
     withdrew the write on a conflict while nothing the value was computed
     from changed (section 4.6).
2. Collect the label identifier of each slot the template reaches under the
   reported selections, the selections themselves, and the children the
   template's `pick` nodes chose. With the slot-free hash of the template
   and the labels of its `dynamic` nodes (section 4.6), this is the
   **instantiation key**. *Assumed,* provisional (P2; section 8, question
   163): the slots, the selections, the chosen children and the `dynamic`
   nodes are those of the nodes that the template itself holds, and for
   each `output` node that the template reaches under those selections
   the key holds the identifier of the label of the named output's
   template ("A label is instantiated once", below). The key of a
   template then has the size of the template as it is written.
   For each `shared` node that the template reaches under those
   selections the key holds, in the same way, the identifier of the
   label of the entry for the inputs of the place, and no slot,
   selection or chosen child of the entry (provisional, P6; section 8,
   question 168).
3. If the key equals the key the stored label was instantiated from, reuse
   that label. A change of value alone ends here.
4. Otherwise instantiate (section 4.2), look the result up in the memo
   (section 4.3), check the constraints (section 4.4), and stage the label
   with the write.

An interim value that is not kept is never labeled: no label is stored
for it and no constraint is checked on it. Its template is not lost.
Every output that depends on it names it, with an `output` node or
through the outputs between them, so its template is a sub-template of
every kept output that depends on it by reference and not by copy. The
label of its template is formed where a template that is instantiated
names it, as the next paragraph says, and is held for the transaction
alone.

**A label is instantiated once.** By ruling the label of an output's
template is evaluated once and used by every template that names the
output, as a memo entry is on the value side.

- **Once per output and set of inputs.** In one transaction the template
  of an output is instantiated at most once for one set of inputs: one
  cone instance, which is one combination of element keys, and under a
  `pick` one chosen child. Every `output` node that names the output for
  that set uses the one result. The same holds where a slot resolves to
  the label of an output's template (sections 2.2 and 3.6), and where
  `TemplateInputs.membership` returns it (section 3.2). The label of
  the membership that a collection iterates, and the label of a
  collection's array that a slot of root `index` resolves to, are
  formed once for the collection and the enclosing keys as well, and
  not once for each element that reads them.
- **Once per entry of the template table and set of inputs.**
  Provisional (P6): in one transaction the label of an entry of
  `Plan.templates` is formed at most once for one set of inputs, by
  steps 2 to 4 for the entry as for a named output, and every `shared`
  node that names the entry for that set uses the one result. A set of
  inputs is a cone instance and under a `pick` a chosen child, as for an
  output. The selections are those of the place that holds the node, and
  one cone instance has one value for each selector, so two positions of
  one cone instance never ask for two labels of one entry. Two write
  edges of one run of a body, and the paths of the result of one call,
  are one set of inputs. No constraint is checked and nothing is staged
  for an entry on its own account: what is stored and checked is the
  label of the template that the transaction instantiates, which holds
  the node.
- **When it is formed.** The label of a named output is formed when step
  2 first needs its identifier, by steps 2 to 4 for that output's own
  template: its key is collected, and the label is looked up in the memo
  or instantiated. No constraint is checked and nothing is staged for an
  interim output on that account. For a kept output that the transaction
  also stores, the one instantiation serves both: the stored label is
  the label of the template with the atom of the kept output added, and
  an `output` node uses it without that atom (section 3.2). Where step 3
  reuses the stored label of a kept output, the label of its template is
  the entry of the memo for the same key.
- **What it costs.** A transaction instantiates each template it needs
  once per set of inputs, and every node of a template once. The cost of
  the label evaluation of a transaction is linear in the number of nodes
  of the templates it instantiates, counted once for each cone instance
  and, provisional (P31), each group of the elements a `fold` covers
  (section 4.2), and does not follow the number of
  paths by which one output depends on another. No rule of this document
  is a walk of a template as a tree that follows `output` nodes without
  this reuse (section 3.2, "A rule over a template").
- **Step 1 for a named output.** The second condition of step 1 follows
  `output` nodes: a demanded output is due where a slot that its
  template reaches, through the outputs it names included, has a new
  label and an unchanged value. Whether an output reaches such a slot is
  found once per output.
- **Between transactions.** Nothing requires the runtime to keep the
  label of an interim output after the transaction. The memo of section
  4.3 returns it from its key. Whether the runtime keeps the key or the
  label identifier of an interim output with the cone instance belongs
  to `execution-and-storage.md`.

**A label that changes alone.** A label can change without its value
changing, when a slot's label changed. *Assumed,* as
`scheduler-and-serving-loop.md` §3.6 proposes and pending the owner's
answer: the second condition of step 1 then holds for a demanded output,
no value code runs, and steps 2 to 4 instantiate the template from the
value and the selections of the last evaluation. The label entry is
rewritten and the constraints are checked again. This is the re-derivation
of §8.9.4 ("When a live reactive node recomputes, the new attempt's journal
sees the source's *current* labels") without the recomputation. An output
nothing demands is not re-instantiated, which that section permits: "There
is **no retroactive relabeling obligation**". Its next evaluation
instantiates with the labels current then. A slot with `sampled` never
makes the second condition hold (section 2.5).

### 4.2 The algorithm

`instantiateTemplate` is a kernel function in the sense of the correspondence
procedure: pure, named after its pseudocode, and the only place the runtime
decides what that pseudocode decides. It takes labels and selections and
returns a label. It takes no transaction and no slot value.

```ts
// Shown for illustration only.
interface TemplateInputs {
  /**
   * Label of a slot, already resolved by address, path and class, with its
   * chain. For an address this transaction or its batch wrote, the label
   * staged there (section 4.5). For a slot of root `index`, the label of
   * the array its collection iterates (section 2.2).
   */
  slotLabel(slot: Index): Label;
  /**
   * The branch the value code took at a selector. For the `through` of a
   * `fold`, the position the runtime's own scan found (section 3.13).
   */
  selection(selector: Index): number;
  /**
   * The distinct groups of the elements of a collection, each one set of
   * element inputs, over the elements up to and including position `upTo`
   * where it is given. Elements whose inputs have equal label identifiers
   * and equal selections are one group (provisional, P31).
   */
  groups(collection: Index, upTo?: number): readonly TemplateInputs[];
  /**
   * The child chosen at a choice point (`Plan.picks`), or undefined when
   * none was chosen.
   */
  chosen(pick: Index): TemplateInputs | undefined;
  /** Label of the membership a collection iterates (section 3.2). */
  membership(collection: Index): Label;
  /**
   * The label of the `template` of an output, for these inputs, without
   * the atom of a kept output. The adapter instantiates it at most once
   * per transaction and set of inputs and returns the same result to
   * every caller (section 4.1). The inputs of an element return the
   * result of the enclosing inputs for an output outside the element
   * body.
   */
  outputLabel(output: Index): Instantiated;
  /**
   * The label of an entry of `Plan.templates` for these inputs. The
   * adapter instantiates the entry at most once per transaction and set
   * of inputs and returns the same result to every caller (section
   * 4.1). Provisional (P6).
   */
  sharedLabel(template: Index): Instantiated;
  /** Join of what a journaled read set consumed. */
  dynamicLabel(reads: Index): Label;
  /**
   * The `TransformedBy` atoms for a derivation, minted by the runtime: for
   * a body, of `Body.code`; for expression code, of the entry of
   * `Plan.patterns` that `pattern` names, or of entry 0.
   */
  mint(
    by: { body: Index } | { expression: true; pattern?: Index },
  ): readonly Atom[];
}

/** What a `const` instantiates to: no clause, and no part in the meet. */
const NEUTRAL = "neutral";
type Instantiated = Label | typeof NEUTRAL;

/**
 * The atoms a `derive` or a `fold` mints, beside a label that has a
 * confidentiality clause or a hereditary atom, and none beside an empty
 * label (ruling of 2026-11-19, section 3.2).
 */
function mintBeside(
  confidentiality: readonly Clause[],
  inherited: readonly Atom[],
  minted: readonly Atom[],
): readonly Atom[] {
  return confidentiality.length > 0 || inherited.length > 0 ? minted : [];
}

function instantiateTemplate(t: Template, inp: TemplateInputs): Instantiated {
  switch (t.op) {
    case "const":
      return NEUTRAL;
    case "slot":
      return inp.slotLabel(t.slot);
    case "output":
      return inp.outputLabel(t.output);
    case "shared":
      return inp.sharedLabel(t.template);
    case "dynamic":
      return inp.dynamicLabel(t.reads);
    case "derive": {
      const parts = t.inputs
        .map((i) => instantiateTemplate(i, inp))
        .filter((l): l is Label => l !== NEUTRAL);
      const confidentiality = joinAll(parts.map((p) => p.confidentiality));
      const inherited = hereditaryMeet(parts.map((p) => p.integrity));
      return {
        confidentiality,
        integrity: [
          ...inherited,
          ...mintBeside(confidentiality, inherited, inp.mint(t.by)),
        ],
      };
    }
    case "select": {
      const cond = instantiateTemplate(t.condition, inp);
      const taken = instantiateTemplate(
        t.branches[inp.selection(t.selector)],
        inp,
      );
      const condConf = cond === NEUTRAL ? [] : cond.confidentiality;
      if (taken === NEUTRAL) {
        return { confidentiality: condConf, integrity: [] };
      }
      return {
        confidentiality: joinAll([condConf, taken.confidentiality]),
        integrity: taken.integrity,
      };
    }
    case "pick": {
      const choice = instantiateTemplate(t.choice, inp);
      const choiceConf = choice === NEUTRAL ? [] : choice.confidentiality;
      const child = inp.chosen(t.pick);
      const taken = child === undefined
        ? NEUTRAL
        : instantiateTemplate(t.body, child);
      if (taken === NEUTRAL) {
        return { confidentiality: choiceConf, integrity: [] };
      }
      return {
        confidentiality: joinAll([choiceConf, taken.confidentiality]),
        integrity: taken.integrity,
      };
    }
    case "fold": {
      const upTo = t.through === undefined
        ? undefined
        : inp.selection(t.through);
      const parts = inp.groups(t.collection, upTo)
        .map((g) => instantiateTemplate(t.body, g))
        .filter((l): l is Label => l !== NEUTRAL);
      const member = inp.membership(t.collection);
      const confidentiality = joinAll([
        member.confidentiality,
        ...parts.map((p) => p.confidentiality),
      ]);
      const inherited = hereditaryMeet(parts.map((p) => p.integrity));
      return {
        confidentiality,
        integrity: [
          ...inherited,
          ...mintBeside(
            confidentiality,
            inherited,
            inp.mint({ expression: true, pattern: t.pattern }),
          ),
        ],
      };
    }
  }
}
```

A `fold` with `through` covers the leading elements up to the position
its selector holds. The runtime supplies that position from its own scan
of the predicate cones (section 3.13): the position of the deciding
element, or the collection's length less one when no element decides, so
that the fold covers everything. The value code reports neither the
selection of a `through` selector nor the position that bounds a prefix
fold.

**Labels by identifier, and a `fold` per group.** Provisional (P31 of the
continuation plan). Inside instantiation a label is handled by its
identifier, the content hash of the normalized label, and the runtime holds
one object per distinct label, so equal labels are one object with one
identifier. A join and a meet are computed over the set of distinct
identifiers of their inputs and memoized by that set: equal inputs cost one
lookup and no comparison of atoms. A `fold` instantiates its body once per
distinct group of element inputs, and not once per element: a group is a set
of label identifiers of the slots the body reads, with the selections, and
`TemplateInputs.groups` returns one set of inputs per group. The cost of a
`fold`'s label in a transaction is then the number of its groups. The
executor reports the elements of a `fold` in a write record in one of two
forms.

- **`uniform`:** one set of slot bindings whose addresses hold the path
  segment `*` at the element's position, and the label of a slot is the
  join of the stored entries that the `*` path covers, one entry in the
  common case (section 2.3, "One entry for the elements of an array written
  whole"). The form is allowed only where the body's template holds no
  `select`, `pick`, `fold`, `dynamic`, `shared` or `output` node below the
  element, because then a join before instantiation equals instantiation
  followed by a join, for confidentiality and for the hereditary meet. It
  is the form for an array of plain values in place.
- **`groups`:** one entry per group, with its bindings, its selections and
  the number of elements that have it. The group of each element key and
  the count per group are kept with the collection's assembly
  (`execution-and-storage.md` §2.5), and are updated when an element is added,
  removed or evaluated again: one update per changed element. It is the
  form for an array of references and for the result of another
  per-element construct.

A label that changes while the value stays the same regroups only the
elements whose group reads a position of the document whose label entry
changed, at, above or below the changed entry, and no other element. Where
a `fold` stands in the body of another `fold`, the group key of an element
of the outer collection holds the set of groups of the inner collection, so
two outer elements whose own inputs are equal are two groups where their
inner folds differ, and a change of the inner set regroups the enclosing
element. For a `fold` with `through` the groups are those of the covered
prefix ("The groups of a prefix", below).

**The groups of a prefix.** *Assumed, provisional (P37;* section 8,
question 183*).* The groups that P31 keeps with a collection's assembly
hold a count per group and no order, so the groups of the elements up to
a position cannot be read from them. A scan (`findIndex`, `some`, `every`,
and the choice of `find`) therefore keeps the group set of its prefix
itself: a count per group over the elements from the first position to the
deciding position, held with the memo entry that holds the scan's position
(section 3.13, "The record of a scan"; `execution-and-storage.md` §3.1).
`TemplateInputs.groups` with `upTo` returns the groups whose count there is
above zero.

- **A change inside the prefix.** An element of the prefix that is
  evaluated again, or whose label changes, takes one from the count of its
  old group and adds one to the count of its new group: one update.
- **A move of the deciding position.** The elements between the old and
  the new position enter or leave the prefix, and each is one update, with
  the group that the collection's assembly holds for its key. A move costs
  the number of elements between the two positions, and not the length of
  the prefix or of the collection.
- **A change of membership before the deciding position.** An element that
  is inserted into or removed from the prefix is one update. A reorder
  changes the counts only for the elements that cross the deciding
  position.
- **No element decides.** The prefix is the whole collection, and its
  groups are those of the collection's assembly. The scan keeps no counts
  of its own until an element decides.
- **After a restart.** The memo is not durable. The scan runs again, and
  the counts are formed again from the groups of the assembly, at the cost
  of the length of the prefix, as the position itself is found again.

By case of the source:

- **An array of references.** The `groups` form. The group of each element
  key is kept with the assembly, and the scan keeps the counts of the
  prefix as above.
- **An array of plain values in place.** The `uniform` form, where the
  predicate's template allows it: one binding whose address holds `*`,
  which covers every element and not the prefix alone. The label of the
  prefix is then the label of all the elements. That is the label of the
  prefix exactly where every element has the one `*` entry of section 2.3,
  and wider where an element behind the deciding position has an entry of
  its own; it is never wider than the read of the whole array that today's
  scan makes. A move of the deciding position costs nothing. Where the
  predicate's template does not allow the `uniform` form, the `groups`
  form applies, as for an array of references.
- **The result of another per-element construct.** The `groups` form, with
  the upstream keys. The slot of an element is bound to the output of the
  upstream element, and the counts of the prefix are kept as for an array
  of references.

The label this gives is the `fold` over the prefix that section 3.13
defines, or in the `uniform` case a label that covers it. The alternative
instantiates the predicate's template for every element of the prefix on
every commit that changes the scan, at the cost of the length of the
prefix.

**Selections and choices that are reported, and the bound where one is
not.** A `select`, a `pick` and a `fold` with `through` instantiate from a
value that the evaluation decided: the branch, the chosen child, the
deciding position. A `dynamic` node instantiates from the addresses that
the evaluation read. Where a write reaches the runtime without one of
them, the runtime does not guess. It takes a bound that covers every
outcome: the join of all branches of a `select`, the join over all
children of a `pick`, the whole collection for a prefix, and the
transaction's join for a `dynamic` node. A bound is equal to or wider than
the label the rule gives, never narrower, so it is sound, and it gives up
the narrowing that the rule exists for. In the ninth run of milestone 4
of the integration over the corpus the runtime took a bound 1,762 times,
in 70 of the 238 modules that run. The count holds two kinds: a write
that reaches the runtime without one of the six reports below, which the
prototype does not make, and a record that the executor gives as bound
because it has no inputs for it, which takes the transaction's join (a
kept output the plan has no template for, an element entry with a slot
that has no stored position, and a member change under an envelope). The
run does not count the two apart. For each report, the table has who
knows the answer, what is reported, and where it is kept between
evaluations, so that a change of a label alone (section 4.1) instantiates
without running value code.

| What is decided | Who knows it | What is reported | Where it is kept |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The child that `h.key(k)` or `h.elementById(k)` chooses, with a key that is not a constant (section 3.18, "Handle methods in the reactive tier") | The value code, which computes `k` | The key, or that no child was chosen, in `ConeResult.picks` for the choice point (`Pick.chosenBy` is `valueCode`), as for `a[k]` | With the memo entry of the cone instance (`execution-and-storage.md` §3.1), and in the provenance record of a kept output (§7.2 there) |
| The deciding position of a scan, the `through` of the `fold` of `findIndex`, `some`, `every` and of the choice of `find` (section 3.13) | The runtime, from its own scan of the per-element predicate outputs | The position, as the selection of the scan's selector of arity 0. No value function reports it | With the memo entry of the scan's result, beside the group counts of the prefix (above) |
| The element that `find` chooses (section 3.13; `Pick.chosenBy` is `runtime`) | The runtime, from the same scan | The key of the chosen element, or that none was chosen, for the choice point | With the memo entry of the scan's result |
| The branch of the `select` that the compiler emits for `a[k]` over a record constructed in place with a static key set (section 3.18, "A container the instance computed") | The value code, which computes `k` | The index of the member that `k` names, or of the last branch where it names none, in `ConeResult.selections` | With the memo entry of the cone instance |
| Whether an optional member of a spread operand is present, the `select` of `{ ...a, x: e }` whose condition is the `shape` of `a.p` (section 3.4, "A spread in an object literal") | The value code, which builds the record and tests the member | The branch, in `ConeResult.selections`: the member of `a`, or the earlier member | With the memo entry of the cone instance |
| The addresses a `dynamic` node of kind `link` read through a reference that a `select` or a `pick` of another cone chose (section 3.10) | The runtime, which resolves the link when the value code reads through the output that holds the reference | The addresses read, with the chain of each, attributed to the node | In the transaction's journal for the evaluation, and for a kept output in the `dynamic` member of its provenance record |

Three of the six are the runtime's own knowledge and need no change of
value code: the deciding position, the chosen element of `find`, and the
addresses of a read through a link. Three are reports that value code
makes in the form it already has for a conditional expression and for a
computed key. The cases of a per-element construct do not differ in who
reports: over an array of references, over an array of plain values in
place and over the result of another per-element construct, the scan and
the choice are the runtime's, and a selection inside the element body is
reported per cone instance, which is per element key.

A template label may rest on the labels of positions that an earlier
transaction observed, as the element inputs of a group do when only one
element changed. By ruling (2026-11-19) that is allowed: such a label is
checked for conflicts at commit, as a read of the committing transaction
is. The runtime records, in the committing transaction, an observation of
the label metadata of each such binding, and no read of its value.
Milestone 4 of the integration records one such observation per group of a
`fold`'s elements.

`instantiateTemplate` returns the label of a template. For a kept output
the adapter adds the atom of entry 0 of `Plan.patterns` to the integrity of
what it returns, a `NEUTRAL` result included (section 3.2, "The atom of the
pattern").

An `output` node does not instantiate the template it names in place.
It asks the adapter for the label, and the adapter calls
`instantiateTemplate` on the named output's template, with the
selections and the chosen children of the cone that computes that
output, the first time the label is asked for in the transaction for
those inputs. It returns what that call returned every time after, a
`NEUTRAL` result included. The function stays pure: the label of an
`output` node is one of its inputs, as the label of a slot is. The
recursion ends because the references among outputs form no cycle
(section 3.2).

A `shared` node does not instantiate its entry in place either
(provisional, P6). It asks the adapter for the label, and the adapter
calls `instantiateTemplate` on the entry of `Plan.templates` with the
inputs that the node was reached with, the selections and the chosen
children of the calling cone included, the first time the label is asked
for in the transaction for those inputs, and returns what that call
returned every time after. The recursion ends because an entry holds
entries smaller than itself alone (section 3.2, "A template written
once").

A `const` instantiates to `NEUTRAL`, and every node that takes a part
handles it. A `derive` and a `fold` leave neutral parts out of the join
and of the meet, so a `derive` over one slot and one literal keeps the
slot's hereditary atoms, and a `derive` with no other input has no
inherited integrity. A `select` or a `pick` whose selected branch or
chosen child is neutral yields the confidentiality of the condition or
of the choice and no integrity, and a neutral condition or choice
contributes no clause.

The adapter around this function gathers the inputs: it resolves each slot's
address to a label through the existing consumed-label index
(`ConsumedLabelIndex`, `runtime/runner/src/cfc/consumed-label-index.ts`),
reads selections from the value code's result, and reads journaled handle and
link reads from the transaction.

### 4.3 Memoization

With labels held by content address
([content-addressed CFC labels](../content-addressed-cfc-labels.md)), a slot
label is an identifier and an instantiation is a function of identifiers:

```text
key   = (template hash, selections, slot label ids in template order,
         label ids of the named outputs in template order,
         label ids of the named entries in template order)
value = label id
```

- The memo is a pure cache, shared across instances and patterns. Template
  hashes are slot-free (section 1.2), so equal templates over different slots
  share entries.
- A `fold` contributes the *set* of its groups' body label identifiers,
  because join and meet are idempotent. Provisional (P31; section 4.2): the
  group of each element key and the count per group are kept with the
  collection's assembly (`execution-and-storage.md` §2.5), not with a durable
  state of the `fold`, so a `fold` that belongs to no operation, such as the
  membership of a `filter` or a `flatMap`, has them as well. Adding,
  removing or evaluating again an element updates them once, and the fold's
  label changes only when a group's count crosses zero or a group's label
  changes. In the `uniform` form there is one group and no count.
- A `dynamic` node contributes the identifiers of the labels its journaled
  reads consumed, and of its trigger reads (section 3.10).
- A slot contributes the identifier of its whole label, the pointer labels
  of its chain included (section 2.5). A `sampled` slot contributes the
  identifier resolved at the cone's last evaluation.
- An `output` node contributes the identifier of the label of the
  template it names, and a neutral result contributes a fixed marker.
  *Assumed,* provisional (P2; section 8, question 163). The label of a
  template is a function of the template as written, its selections, the
  labels of its slots and the labels of the outputs it names, so the
  entry is as pure as one keyed by every slot the named templates reach.
  Two templates that are equal as written share entries whatever the
  templates of the outputs they name are, where those have equal labels.
- A `shared` node contributes the identifier of the label of its entry
  for the inputs of the place, and a neutral result contributes a fixed
  marker. *Assumed,* provisional (P6; section 8, question 168). The
  selections, the slots and the chosen children of the entry are in the
  entry's own key and not in the key of a template that names it. The
  entry is as pure for the reason given for an `output` node: the label
  of a template is a function of the template as written, its own
  selections and slot labels, and the labels of what it names.
- That design holds label identifiers only above an inline size limit
  (`CFC_LABEL_INLINE_LIMIT` in `runtime/runner/src/cfc/label-documents.ts`).
  The memo key uses the hash of the label either way; whether the stored
  entry holds the label inline or by reference is unchanged.

For a `map` over `n` elements whose body has one template, `n` elements with
equal slot labels are one memo entry and one stored `*`-child entry, over an
array of plain values in place, an array of references and the result of
another per-element construct alike (section 2.3, "One entry for the
elements of an array written whole", for when the `*` entry is stored). This
is also what makes the binding of element slots per key (section 1.3) cheap:
keys whose slot labels are equal have one label.

### 4.4 Constraints

A constraint that today is checked against a transaction's reads becomes a
constraint on the inputs of a body or on a write edge.

| Constraint | Today | In the plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `requiredIntegrity` on an input path | `verifyInputRequirements` over the reads before the last overlapping write | `I` of each listed input satisfies the patterns, with one coherent witness across them |
| `maxConfidentiality` on an input path | Same function, same read set | `⊔` of `C` over the listed inputs fits the ceiling |
| Write floor on a target | `verifyWriteFloor` on the written value's integrity | `I(template)` of the write edge satisfies the patterns |
| Writer-fit | Persist region of `prepareBoundaryCommitSteps`: the join fits the target's declared confidentiality | `C(template)` of the write edge fits it |
| `writeAuthorizedBy`, `writePolicyAnyOf` | `writeAuthorizedByReason`, `writePolicyAnyOfReason` at prepare | `Body.code` of the writing body is one the policy names |
| UI event integrity contract | `verifyTrustedEventRequirements` (`runtime/runner/src/cfc/prepare.ts`), with provenance recorded by `recordTrustedEventPolicyInputs` (`runtime/runner/src/cfc/ui-contract.ts`) | The event bound to the handler's `event` root satisfies the alternative's `uiContract`, checked per event (below) |
| Egress ceiling of an effect | `verifySinkRequestCeilings` over the whole transaction's consumed label | `C` of the request's templates, joined with what following the references the request holds consumes, as far as the effect serializes or hashes them, fits the ceiling. For each later send of the effect, `C` of everything that send serializes fits the ceiling (section 3.14) |

**What an input constraint lists.** A `requiredIntegrity` or a
`maxConfidentiality` constraint lists the inputs of the body's footprint
whose path overlaps the annotated path, in either prefix direction, which
is the overlap the runtime uses today (`buildWritePrefixBounds`). A body
reads an annotated path in three ways, and the constraint lists each
(`ConstraintInputs`).

- **Through a slot of `Body.reads`.** The constraint lists the slot
  (`slots`), and is evaluated on the slot's label.
- **Through an entry of `Body.handles`,** where the read is dynamic. The
  constraint lists the entry with the annotated path below the handle's
  cell (`handles`). It is evaluated on the journaled reads made through
  the entry whose path overlaps that path: on the label each of those
  reads consumed. The read envelope keeps the label annotations of the
  paths it admits (`footprint-analysis.md` §7.3), so a read through the
  entry is known to be at an annotated path. On a run that made no such
  read the entry contributes nothing, as an attempt with no such read
  contributes nothing today.
- **In a value the instance computed,** an entry of `Body.computed`. The
  constraint lists the entry (`computed`), and is evaluated on the
  entry's template, instantiated.

`requiredIntegrity` requires the patterns of the integrity of each of
these, and `maxConfidentiality` tests the join of the confidentiality of
all of them. A constraint that lists nothing is not emitted: an
annotation on a path the body does not read constrains nothing. Today
the gate quantifies over the journaled reads of the transaction, the
ones made through cells included, so the three forms together are what
it covers.

**Where a constraint comes from.** `language-subset.md` §8.1 lists the keys
a label annotation adds to a type. The plan holds each as follows.

| Annotation key | In the plan |
| --- | --- |
| `confidentiality` | `Slot.declared.confidentiality` of a slot the annotation covers (`language-subset.md` §8.3), and a declared entry of the stored label (section 2.3). On a path a write edge targets, it is the declared confidentiality a `writerFit` constraint tests the edge's template against |
| `integrity` | `Slot.declared.integrity` of a slot the annotation covers, and a declared entry of the stored label |
| `requiredIntegrity` | A `requiredIntegrity` constraint with the annotation's patterns, over the slots that overlap the annotated path. On a path a write edge targets, *assumed* (section 8, question 15), also a `writeFloor` constraint with the same patterns |
| `maxConfidentiality` | A `maxConfidentiality` constraint with the annotation's ceiling, over the slots that overlap the annotated path |
| `writeAuthorizedBy` | A `writer` constraint on each write edge to the annotated path, with one `WriterPolicy` whose `body` is the body the binding names |
| `writePolicyAnyOf` | A `writer` constraint on each write edge to the annotated path, with one `WriterPolicy` per policy of the list |
| `uiContract` | `WriterPolicy.uiContract` of the alternative it is declared with |
| `addIntegrity`, `exactCopyOf`, `projection` | No record and no rule (section 8, question 14) |

A kept output at the annotated path has each of these constraints as a
write edge to the path has (section 1.5): `writerFit`, `writer` and
`writeFloor`. That `requiredIntegrity` is the key of a write floor is
the assumption of question 15 of section 8.

**When a constraint is checked.**

- **At compile time**, when everything it reads is declared: every listed
  slot has a `declared` label for the dimension the constraint tests, or the
  constraint is about a body's identity. A violation is a compile error that
  names the slot and the annotation. The writer policy is always checkable at
  compile time for a static write edge, because both the body and the policy
  are in the source.
- **At instantiation** otherwise, with the labels the template was
  instantiated from. What a failure does depends on whose write the
  constraint guards (below).
- **Per event** for a UI contract. A write that a `writer` constraint
  admits through an alternative with a `uiContract` is admitted only
  where the event the handler was invoked with satisfies that contract:
  it came from an element under the surface the contract names, with the
  action and the event integrity the contract requires. The check is a
  check on what the handler itself writes, so a failure rejects the
  event's transaction. Whether an event came from the named
  surface is a fact about that event (`trustedEventProvenanceMatchesUiContract`
  in `runtime/runner/src/cfc/ui-contract.ts`). The compiler reports, as a
  warning (`cfc-flow:ui-contract`, `language-subset.md` §10.5), the case
  where no element of the compiled pattern that binds the handler sits under
  a surface carrying the required pattern and integrity names, since then no
  event from this pattern's UI can satisfy the policy. It is not an error,
  because a handler bound to an exported stream also receives events from
  other patterns (section 6.3 has one).

**What `cfc-flow:ui-contract` reads.** The check needs no record beyond
the plan's and the rendered tree of the source. Today the renderer forms
an event's UI provenance from the element a listener is bound on and the
elements above it (`getEventProvenance` and `getEventUiProvenance` in
`runtime/html/src/main/event-provenance.ts`), and the compiler reads the
same three attributes from the JSX the pattern writes.

- **An element binds a handler** where an `on*` attribute of a host
  element holds the stream of an entry of `Plan.bindings` whose body is
  the handler, an element of a pattern compiled into the plan included.
- **The chain of an element** is the element and the host elements that
  enclose it in the JSX of the plan, outward through the callbacks of
  element constructs and the branches of a selection, to the root of
  the tree the element is written in. Whether it continues from that
  root depends on how the tree reaches a renderer ("Where a chain
  continues", below). The `UiAction`, `UiPromptSlot` and
  `UiDisclosure` helpers are host elements with the data attribute each
  one sets (`createUiHelper` in `runtime/runner/src/builder/h.ts`).
- **The surface of an element** has three parts. Its pattern is the
  value of `data-ui-pattern` on the nearest element of the chain that
  has the attribute. Its integrity names are the names in
  `data-ui-event-integrity` of every element of the chain, each value
  split at white space and commas. Its contract attributes are those
  of the nearest element of the chain that has any of `data-ui-action`,
  `data-ui-surface`, `data-ui-role` and `data-ui-disclosure-kind`.
- **An element satisfies a `uiContract`** where the contract's
  `trustedPattern`, if it has one, is the surface's pattern, every name
  of `requiredEventIntegrity` is among the surface's integrity names,
  and, for the helper `UiAction`, the contract's `action` is the value
  of `data-ui-action` among the contract attributes. This is
  `recordedTrustedEventProvenanceMatchesUiContract`
  (`runtime/runner/src/cfc/ui-contract.ts`) over what the renderer
  would record for the element. `WriterPolicy.uiContract` has no member
  for the surface and the role of `UiPromptSlot` or the kind of
  `UiDisclosure`, so an alternative with one of those helpers is not
  decided.

**Where a chain continues.** At run time the surface of an event is read
from the rendered document (`getEventUiProvenance`), whichever pattern
wrote each element of it. An element one pattern writes can therefore
sit under a surface that another pattern writes. The compiler follows a
chain past the root of a tree in one case.

- **A pattern compiled into the plan by a JSX tag** (a `site` step whose
  call is a tag). The tag's position in the enclosing tree holds the
  callee's `[UI]` (section 1.1). The chain of an element of the callee's
  tree continues at the tag's position, with the elements that enclose
  the tag, and through every further tag of this kind. In
  `patterns/product/lobby/main.tsx` the tag `LobbyParticipantRow` is
  written in the callback of a `map` under the `cf-screen` that carries
  the surface, so the chain of a button of the row reaches that element.
- **A pattern compiled into the plan by a call** (a `site` step whose
  call is `Row({ ... })` in the reactive tier). The callee's tree is the
  path `$UI` of the call's result, a value of the plan. It reaches a
  renderer wherever that value is placed: at a child position of the
  enclosing tree, in the result for another pattern to place, or
  through a body. In `patterns/system/fabrichat/room.tsx` the trees of
  the `FabriChatThreadComposer` calls are collected by a `computed` and
  placed under the element that carries the surface. *Assumed* (section
  8, question 61): the compiler does not follow the value, and the chain
  ends at the root of the callee's tree.
- **A pattern with a plan of its own.** The plan of a pattern holds its
  own JSX and nothing of a tree that embeds its result: a `Child` is
  instantiated at run time, and a pattern another module instantiates
  is compiled without that module. The chain ends at the root of the
  pattern's tree.
- **An element that is an argument, or a tree that is no pattern's
  `[UI]`.** An element written between the tags of a pattern, or in an
  attribute of one, is a value of the callee's argument, and the callee
  decides where it is rendered. A tree held in a constant or computed
  as a value is placed by a reference. The compiler follows neither,
  and the surface of an element in such a tree is not decided.

**When the warning is reported.** It is reported for a handler and an
alternative with a `uiContract` where the plan has at least one element
that binds the handler, none of them satisfies the contract, and the
surface of each is decided. A surface is decided where all of the
following hold: every one of those attributes on its chain is a
constant, in the sense section 3.19 gives the operands of `wish`; no
element of the chain has a spread attribute; every tag on the chain
names a host element, one of the three helpers, or a pattern compiled
in by that tag; and the element is not in a tree of the last case
above. Where a surface is not decided, and where no element of the plan
binds the handler, the compiler is silent.

A chain that ends at the root of a pattern's tree is decided on the
elements it has. So a pattern that binds a trusted action and leaves the
surface to the pattern that embeds it is reported, whether it has a
plan of its own or is compiled in by a call, although an event from the
embedded tree satisfies the contract at run time. *Assumed* (section 8,
question 61): it is reported, as the warning it is. The check is made
once per plan. A pattern that has no plan of its own is checked in each
plan it is compiled into, and nowhere else. Provisional (P18): for a
callee that is compiled in by a tag the check is per call site, because
the chain continues at the position of the tag. *Assumed:* it is
computed once per record and site and not once per chain of sites:
whether a chain is satisfied below the root of a callee's tree is found
once for the callee, and whether it is satisfied from the position of a
tag upward once for the site.

A compile-time check does not replace the run-time one. Declared labels are a
lower bound on what a slot carries: a derived component can add
confidentiality the schema does not declare (§8.12.8). So a compile-time pass
on `maxConfidentiality` settles nothing, and only a compile-time *failure* is
reported: a clause the declaration states that the ceiling does not admit.
For `requiredIntegrity` and the write floor a declared atom that satisfies
the pattern does settle it for the slot, because the slot has every atom
its declaration states. "The relations a constraint tests" and "What the
compiler decides", below, state the relations and the cases.

**The relations a constraint tests.** Four relations decide the label
constraints. Each is stated here over labels as data, so that the
compiler and the runtime evaluate one definition. The runtime functions
named are the ones that hold each relation today, and the specification
states them in §8.10.3 (`08-10-validation-at-boundaries.md`), §8.12.4 and
§8.12.4.1 (`08-12-store-label-monotonicity.md`), and §4.3.3
(`04-label-representation.md`).

A confidentiality label is a list of clauses. A clause is an atom, or
`{ anyOf: [...] }` with a list of atoms, its **alternatives**. An atom
that is no such record is a clause with itself as its one alternative. A
ceiling is a list of clauses too. An integrity label is a list of atoms,
and a required integrity is a list of patterns.

- **An atom `a` entails an atom `b`** where the two are structurally
  equal, or where both are `Expires` atoms with exactly the members
  `type` and `timestamp`, the timestamps are finite numbers, and the
  timestamp of `a` is at most that of `b` (`atomEntails` in
  `runtime/runner/src/cfc/atom-pattern.ts`). The runtime adds equality
  across a committed field, which no label a compiler reads holds.
- **A ceiling clause subsumes a label clause** where the ceiling clause
  has at least one alternative, and every alternative of it entails some
  alternative of the label clause. One case is added on the label's
  side: an alternative `{ type: PersonalSpace, owner }`, with those two
  members alone, also counts as `{ type: User, subject: owner }`
  (`clauseSubsumes` in `runtime/runner/src/cfc/clause.ts`).
- **A label fits a ceiling** where every clause of the label is subsumed
  by some clause of the ceiling. A clause that holds the marker of a
  failed label read fits no ceiling (`atomsOutsideCeiling` and
  `cfcObservationFitsCeiling` in
  `runtime/runner/src/cfc/observation.ts`). The empty label fits every
  ceiling, and the empty ceiling admits the empty label alone. An absent
  ceiling is no constraint.
- **A pattern matches an atom** by the structural match of
  `matchAtomPattern` (`runtime/runner/src/cfc/atom-pattern.ts`): a
  scalar pattern matches the equal scalar; an array pattern matches an
  array of the same length member by member; a record pattern matches a
  record that has every member the pattern names, each matched in turn,
  whatever other members the record has; a member the pattern gives as
  `undefined` requires the record to lack it; and a variable matches any
  value, the same value at each of its occurrences in one pattern.
- **An atom satisfies a required pattern** where the pattern matches it
  or the atom entails the pattern (`integrityAtomSatisfies` in
  `observation.ts`). A pattern of the form `{ type: Concept, uri }` is
  different: it is satisfied by a concrete atom that reaches the concept
  in the trust closure of the acting principal, which is a fact of the
  run (§4.8.9, `04-label-representation.md`).
- **An integrity label satisfies a required integrity** where every
  pattern is satisfied by some atom of the label
  (`cfcIntegritySatisfiesFloor`).
- **Several integrity labels satisfy a required integrity coherently**
  where, for every pattern, one atom satisfies it in every one of the
  labels. Two atoms are one witness where they are structurally equal,
  and an atom whose `scope` has a `valueRef` is compared without its
  `scope.projection` (`cfcIntegritySatisfiesFloorCoherently` and
  `cfcIntegrityWitnessKey`). With no label the requirement holds, and
  with one label the relation is the one above.

The constraints use them as follows.

| Constraint | Holds where |
| --- | --- |
| `maxConfidentiality` | The join of `C` over the listed inputs fits `ceiling`. A join of labels fits a ceiling exactly where each of them does, which is how `verifyInputRequirements` tests it, read by read |
| `requiredIntegrity` | The integrity labels of the listed inputs, one label per input, satisfy `patterns` coherently |
| `writeFloor` | `I(template)` of the write satisfies `patterns`. Where the edge has a `reference`, the label is the integrity of the referenced value, since `verifyWriteFloor` holds each link written at the path to the floor by the label of what it links to |
| `writerFit` | `C(template)` of the write fits the ceiling formed from the confidentiality declared at the target and the **residency clauses** of the target document: `{ type: Space, space }` with the document's space, `{ type: PersonalSpace, owner }` with that space for a document of scope `space`, and `{ type: User, subject }` with the principal of the scope instance for a document of scope `user` or `session`. A target that declares no confidentiality has the residency clauses alone (the persist region of `prepareBoundaryCommitSteps`) |

Before the runtime tests a fit it evaluates the exchange rules of the
deployment over the label, which can add alternatives to a clause
(`evaluateAccessExchange` in `prepare.ts`; §5.3,
`05-policy-architecture.md`). The fit is tested on the label so
rewritten. The relation is the same, and the rewriting is a fact of the
run.

**What the compiler decides.** The compiler evaluates a constraint on
declared labels: each `slot` node of a template stands for the
`declared` member of the slot in the dimension tested, in the canonical
data form of `language-subset.md` §8.5. It evaluates a template by the
table of section 3.2, with these rules.

- A template is evaluated only where every `slot` node it reaches, on
  every selection, has the `declared` member of the dimension tested,
  and it has no `dynamic`, `fold` or `pick` node. An input constraint is
  evaluated only where it lists no entry of `handles`. An `output` node
  evaluates to what the template it names evaluates to, and is not
  evaluated where that template is not. The compiler evaluates the
  template of an output once and uses the result at every node that
  names it (section 3.2, "A rule over a template").
- **A write of a body that holds a handle is not decided.** The template
  of every write edge of a body, and of every output it derives, is a
  `derive` over all of `Body.reads` (section 3.2). The plan holds that
  `derive` once, as an entry of `Plan.templates` where it stands at more
  than one position (provisional, P6), and the rule of this item is
  decided once for the entry. A body that writes through a handle has
  the `identity` slot of that handle among them (`footprint-analysis.md`
  §6.1), and an `identity` slot has no `declared` member (section 1.5).
  By the rule above the template is then not evaluated. So
  `cfc-flow:writer-fit` and `cfc-flow:write-floor` are never decided for
  a write a handler, an action or a computation makes through a handle,
  nor for any other write or output of a body whose footprint has an
  `identity` slot or a `shape` slot in place. The runtime checks each of
  them at instantiation. The compiler decides the two for an output or
  an edge whose template reaches only slots that have a declared label:
  expression code over `value`, `shape` and `enumeration` slots, and a
  body that reads values and holds no handle. `cfc-flow:write-policy`
  and `cfc-flow:ui-contract` read no label, and are decided for a write
  through a handle as for any other. *Assumed* (section 8, question 60):
  this stands.
- **A slot of root `event` is not decided on.** The plan records
  `Slot.declared` for such a slot, and it is no lower bound of the slot's
  label, which is the label the event arrived with (section 3.12). For
  the rule above the slot counts as one with no `declared` member, in
  both dimensions: a template that reaches it is not evaluated, and an
  input constraint that lists it is not decided. The runtime checks each
  at instantiation, on the label the event arrived with.
- An atom, a clause or a pattern that holds a term bound at run time is
  not compared. The terms are the `CurrentPrincipal` marker, the atom of
  a `PolicyOf` term, and a `Concept` pattern. How much is left undecided
  depends on where the term is. A clause of the lower bound, or a
  required pattern, that holds one is left out, and the check is decided
  on the other clauses and patterns: each clause has to fit by itself
  and each pattern has to be satisfied by itself, so the one left out
  cannot make another pass. A term in the ceiling, in the
  confidentiality declared at a target, or in an integrity atom of an
  input leaves the whole constraint undecided, because once the term is
  bound that clause could admit, or that atom satisfy, any of the
  others.
- **Atoms as data.** The `type` of an atom is compared as the string it
  is. The types the relations name, `Expires`, `User`, `PersonalSpace`,
